findings.plain: People whose genes make them carry more EBV appear somewhat more likely to get ME/CFS in one large dataset but not clearly in another. This is a weak hint that EBV control matters.
findings.detail: A Solving ME/CFS Mendelian randomisation re-analysis used EBV load instruments from Kamitaki 2026 (n≈655k). It gave a combined OR of about 1.23 (p≈0.02), and HLA instruments at r²<0.01 held (p=0.012, 0.043). HLA patterns that raise antibodies to the lytic EBV proteins ZEBRA and EA-D also align with higher risk, but negative-control serologies (VZV, HHV-6B) align similarly, so the HLA signal is not EBV-specific. Genetic correlation of ME/CFS with infectious mononucleosis was 0.11 ± 0.14, and with EBV load 0.05 ± 0.04, both non-significant. Reverse MR was underpowered. Not yet replicated by an independent group.

studies.cite: Solving ME/CFS re-analysis (genetics_mr), using Kamitaki 2026 instruments, DecodeME and MVP
studies.result: EBV load OR 1.13 (DecodeME, ns), 1.59 (MVP, p=0.012)

contradicting.result: VZV and HHV-6B HLA instruments also align, undermining EBV specificity

open_questions: Does the signal hold with full Kamitaki summary statistics and the larger DecodeME release?
Is it the MHC driving everything?

findings.finding: Antibodies against herpesvirus dUTPases (EBV, HHV-6, VZV), proposed as a marker of lytic or abortive-lytic reactivation, are higher in ME/CFS in studies from one lab, including a 2026 longitudinal study (873 serum samples, 40 patients vs 16 controls) where levels tracked fatigue severity.
findings.plain: One research group measures antibodies to a viral enzyme made when herpesviruses partly wake up. They repeatedly find more of these antibodies in ME/CFS, but other labs have not yet checked.
findings.detail: Halpin 2017: 30.9-52.7% of ME/CFS patients had antibodies to multiple herpesviral and/or human dUTPases vs 17.2% of controls, and anti-EBV dUTPase was higher in ME/CFS. Palomo 2026 (J Med Virol): longitudinal sampling, with EBV/HHV-6/VZV dUTPase IgG significantly higher (p<0.001). 72.5% of patients co-expressed antibodies to multiple herpesvirus and HERV-K dUTPases vs 31% of controls, and EBV and HHV-6 dUTPase IgG correlated with fatigue. The controls were few (n=16). In healthy cohorts positivity ranges from 40-84% and rises with age (Alharshawi 2022), so baseline rates are high. The assays are not commercial, and all data come from the Ariza lab.

studies.n: ME/CFS and GWI cohorts vs controls
studies.result: multiple dUTPase antibodies 31-53% vs 17%; anti-EBV dUTPase higher
EBV/HHV-6/VZV dUTPase IgG higher (p<0.001); correlated with fatigue

contradicting.result: 40-84% of asymptomatic people have anti-dUTPase antibodies; higher with age

open_questions: Independent replication with blinded samples?
Does dUTPase protein itself (an immune modulator via TLR2) circulate during crashes?

findings.finding: Serologic evidence of recent EBV reactivation (EA-D IgG) is associated with long COVID fatigue (OR 2.12) in a 280-person cohort, consistent with an earlier small report.
findings.plain: People with long COVID more often have antibody signs that EBV recently reactivated, which may be one route by which COVID leads to lasting illness.
findings.detail: Peluso 2023 (JCI, n=280): LC fatigue and neurocognitive symptoms were associated with EA-D IgG positivity or high EBNA IgG, independent of covariates, but not with EBV viremia. Prior CMV infection was associated with lower LC risk. Gold 2021 (n=68) reported 66.7% of LC vs 10% of controls positive for EA-D IgG or VCA IgM, a small study with a convenience control group. Cervia-Hasler 2024 found classical complement activation linked to higher herpesvirus antibody titres in active LC. Serology cannot distinguish a cause of LC from a consequence of a general immune disturbance.

studies.result: EA-D IgG associated with fatigue (OR 2.12); no association with viremia; CMV seropositivity protective
EBV reactivation serology 66.7% vs 10%

open_questions: Do people with ME/CFS (non-COVID) show the same EA-D pattern at onset?
Is reactivation sustained or a one-off after acute COVID?
findings.test_available: EBV EA-D IgG is clinically available; interpretation is non-specific.

findings.finding: In active long COVID, classical complement pathway activation tracked raised antibody titres against several herpesviruses, alongside markers of haemolysis, platelet activation and monocyte-platelet aggregates.
findings.plain: In long COVID, the blood's complement defence system stays switched on, and this goes along with higher antibodies to herpesviruses. One explanation is that immune complexes against reactivated viruses keep complement firing.
findings.detail: Cervia-Hasler 2024 (Science) ran proteomics on >6,500 proteins in 268 longitudinal samples from Zurich/Basel cohorts followed to 12 months. Active LC showed terminal complement dysregulation and ongoing alternative and classical pathway activation, and the classical arm was associated with increased anti-herpesvirus (e.g., EBV, CMV) titres. Machine learning put complement and thromboinflammation proteins at the top. The cohort was mostly post-hospital-era COVID. No ME/CFS (non-COVID) replication yet. Complement activation fits several mechanisms, and herpes reactivation is only one of them.

studies.result: complement dysregulation in active LC; classical activation associated with herpesvirus antibody titres

open_questions: Does the herpes-complement association appear in classic ME/CFS?
Would antivirals reduce complement activation in LC?
findings.test_available: Complement panels (C3, C4, CH50, sC5b-9) are clinically available but not validated for LC/ME/CFS.

findings.finding: HHV-6 microRNA (miR-aU14) was detected by in situ hybridisation in brain and spinal cord tissue from 3 ME/CFS post-mortem donors but not in 24 controls (Kasimir 2022).
findings.plain: A small autopsy study found signs of active HHV-6 in the brain and spinal cord of three people with ME/CFS and none in controls. This needs repeating in many more brains.
findings.detail: Kasimir 2022 (Front Mol Biosci) used FISH against an HHV-6 miRNA in frontal lobe, basal ganglia and spinal cord from 3 ME/CFS donors, 3 disease controls and 21 Cambridge Brain Bank controls. The authors also report evidence of EBV activity in tissue. Limitations: n=3 cases, no blinding is described in the abstract, miRNA FISH specificity in post-mortem tissue, and no quantitative PCR or sequencing confirmation. The authors argue that blood negativity in many studies reflects localised tissue reactivation. In vitro, HHV-6 reactivation from integrated genomes fragments mitochondria and induces an antiviral state, and patient serum transferred a similar effect (Schreiner 2020, Immunohorizons).

studies.result: HHV-6 miR-aU14 in brain/spinal cord only in ME/CFS
HHV-6 reactivation fragments mitochondria, inhibits PDH and FAO; induces antiviral state

contradicting.result: no HHV-6 seroprevalence difference
HHV-6 DNA in PBMC 82.8% vs 82%; plasma 1.7% vs 0%

open_questions: Blinded multi-site replication in brain banks (e.g., with ME/CFS tissue now being collected)?
Is reactivated HHV-6 cause or consequence of illness?
findings.test_available: research only (blood HHV-6 PCR is available but generally uninformative)

findings.finding: Inherited chromosomally integrated HHV-6 (iciHHV-6, ~1% of people) has been reported at roughly twice the population rate in a neurological/fatigue clinic cohort, but this has not been confirmed in a large ME/CFS sample.
findings.plain: About 1 in 100 people are born with HHV-6 built into one of their chromosomes. One small study suggested this is more common in ME/CFS, and the large UK DecodeME study is checking.
findings.detail: A 2013 University of South Florida study reported iciHHV-6 in >2% of adults with CFS and neurological symptoms vs ~0.8% population estimates. It was a small, selected clinic cohort, and the information here comes from secondary reports only. UK prevalence is about 1.4%, rising to ~3% in parts of Scotland and Ireland, so ancestry confounding matters. DecodeME has an approved sub-study to measure iciHHV-6 in ~4,500 participants, comparing infection-onset vs other onsets. No published result had been found as of this review. iciHHV-6 can produce false 'high HHV-6 DNA' results on commercial PCR panels, a common source of misinterpretation.

studies.result: >2% iciHHV-6 vs ~0.8% population
pending

open_questions: Is iciHHV-6 enriched in DecodeME, and especially in infection-onset cases?
Does integrated-genome reactivation occur in patients' tissues?
findings.test_available: Hair-follicle or nail HHV-6 PCR / ddPCR ratio of viral to cellular genomes can confirm iciHHV-6 (specialist labs).

findings.finding: Enteroviral VP1 protein was found in stomach biopsies from 82% of 165 CFS patients vs 20% of controls, with EV RNA in 37% vs 5%, but this has not been independently replicated with blinded methods.
findings.plain: One clinician-researcher found enterovirus protein in the stomach lining of most patients he biopsied. Other labs have not confirmed it, and the antibody stain used may cross-react.
findings.detail: Chia 2008 (J Clin Pathol): 135/165 consecutive CFS patients' antrum biopsies stained positive for VP1 in parietal cells vs 7/34 controls (p≤0.001), and EV RNA was found in 9/24 vs 1/21 paraffin samples. Paired samples taken years apart stayed positive. The patients were the author's own referral population. The controls were biopsies taken for other gastric conditions, and the 5D8/1 VP1 antibody has known cross-reactivity concerns. Earlier muscle work found EV RNA in 41/158 postviral fatigue vs 2/152 controls (Bowles 1993), but later muscle studies were inconsistent. O'Neal & Hanson 2021 concluded the methods used were inadequate either to confirm or to rule out persistent EV infection, and a Cornell EV-targeted RNA-seq thesis (2022) detected no EVs in patients or controls.

studies.result: VP1 82% vs 20%; EV RNA 37% vs 5%

contradicting.result: prior methods inadequate; evidence neither confirms nor excludes persistent EV
no EV detected in ME/CFS or controls
no enterovirus RNA

open_questions: Blinded, multi-lab testing of gastric/intestinal tissue with sequencing-based detection of non-cytolytic (5' terminally deleted) EV RNA?
Do historical ME outbreaks (e.g., Royal Free 1955) fit EV epidemiology?
findings.test_available: research only (stomach VP1 staining available from one private practice; not validated)

findings.finding: SARS-CoV-2 spike, S1 or nucleocapsid antigen is detectable in plasma more often after COVID than in pre-pandemic samples (excess +11% at 3-6 months, +5.4% at 10-14 months), with more antigenemia after more severe acute illness.
findings.plain: In about 1 in 10 people, bits of the virus can still be found in the blood months after COVID, which suggests a hidden reservoir. Whether this causes long COVID is less certain.
findings.detail: Peluso 2024 (Lancet Infect Dis; 171 post-COVID vs 250 pre-pandemic controls, Simoa) found 2% assay positivity in pre-pandemic controls. Antigenemia was associated with hospitalisation and worse acute illness. The association with LC symptoms was modest and not consistent across all symptom groups (detail from secondary reports). Swank 2022/23 (n=63) reported spike in a majority of PASC patients up to 12 months, a small sample later tempered by larger work. In PAX LC, circulating S1/spike levels did not change after 15 days of nirmatrelvir (Bhattacharjee 2026 preprint).

studies.result: excess antigen prevalence +11%, +8.7%, +5.4% at 3-6, 6-10, 10-14 months

studies.cite: Swank 2022, medRxiv (later published in Clin Infect Dis)
studies.result: spike detected in most PASC patients up to 12 months

contradicting.result: circulating S1/spike unchanged after nirmatrelvir
no persistent antigen
Blood transcriptomics did not support SARS-CoV-2 persistence in post-COVID condition with chronic fatigue syndrome (title; abstract not available)

open_questions: Is antigenemia from replicating virus, translated persistent RNA, or slow-clearing protein?
Does antigen positivity identify an antiviral-responsive LC subgroup?

findings.finding: SARS-CoV-2 RNA and protein persist in gut and other tissues for months to two years in a minority of people, and in a Beijing tissue study, viral RNA in tissue was associated with long COVID symptoms (OR 5.17).
findings.plain: Viral genetic material can hide in the gut and other organs long after the nose test is negative. Several groups have now seen this, and people with long COVID seem to have it more often.
findings.detail: Zollner 2022 (n=46 IBD patients, ~7 months): gut mucosal RNA in 32/46 and nucleocapsid in 24/46, associated with post-acute symptoms. Natarajan 2022 (n=113): fecal RNA in 12.7% at 4 months and 3.8% at 7 months, linked to GI symptoms. Zuo 2024 (Lancet ID; 317 samples from 225 patients): RNA in 30%/27%/11% of solid tissues at 1/2/4 months, with tissue RNA associated with LC symptoms (OR 5.17). Peluso 2024 (Sci Transl Med; n=24 PET) found T-cell activation (F-AraG) in gut wall and spinal cord linked to LC, and RNA in rectosigmoid tissue up to 676 days in some participants. These are mostly convenience tissue samples, and some people without LC also carry RNA.

studies.result: gut RNA 32/46, nucleocapsid 24/46 at ~7 months
fecal RNA 12.7% at 4 months, 3.8% at 7 months; linked to GI symptoms
tissue RNA 30%/27%/11%; associated with LC (OR 5.17)
T-cell activation in gut/spinal cord with LC; gut RNA up to ~2 years

open_questions: Do tissue reservoirs exist in non-COVID ME/CFS for other viruses?
Why do antivirals not help if reservoirs exist (wrong drug, too short, too late, or reservoir not causal)?

findings.finding: Three randomised placebo-controlled trials of 15-25 days of nirmatrelvir-ritonavir in established long COVID (STOP-PASC n=155, PAX LC n=100, RECOVER-VITAL n=959; about 1,214 people in total) found no benefit on primary or secondary outcomes.
findings.plain: Paxlovid, the COVID antiviral, has been tested several times in people who already have long COVID, and it did not help.
findings.detail: STOP-PASC (Geng 2024, JAMA IM): 15 days, 2:1 randomisation, no difference in pooled severity of 6 symptoms at 10 weeks; mostly vaccinated participants, mean 17.5 months after infection. PAX LC (Sawano 2025, Lancet ID): adjusted PROMIS-29 physical difference -0.55 (p=0.54). RECOVER-VITAL (Baden 2026, Lancet ID; 69 sites): 15- or 25-day regimens, no benefit in cognitive, autonomic or exercise phenotypes. All were safe apart from dysgeusia. Caveats: participants were not selected for antigenemia or reservoir evidence, illness was long-standing, and the drug's tissue penetration is uncertain. Ensitrelvir was also null per a secondary summary.

studies.result: no difference in core symptom severity at 10 weeks
PROMIS-29 PHSS difference -0.55 (95% CI -2.32 to 1.21)
no benefit in any phenotype

open_questions: Would trials enriched for antigen-positive participants, or using longer/combination antivirals or monoclonal antibodies, differ?

findings.finding: Treating acute COVID-19 with nirmatrelvir may reduce later long COVID: a small terminated Norwegian RCT found 26% vs 43% at 3 months (RR 0.60), echoing observational VA data, but larger prospective evidence is lacking.
findings.plain: Taking the antiviral early, while COVID is still active, might lower the chance of developing long COVID, but the only trial so far was small and stopped early.
findings.detail: PANORAMIC Norway (Oppegaard 2026, Lancet ID): enrolled 144 of a planned 2,000 before stopping for poor recruitment, and found long COVID in 17/66 vs 33/77 (RR 0.60, 95% CI 0.37-0.98, p=0.039). An unblinding effect via dysgeusia (86% vs 18%) is possible because the outcomes were self-reported. VA cohort (Xie 2023, JAMA IM; 35,717 treated vs 246,076) reported lower risk, while Fung 2023 (older Medicare patients) found no reduction. Metformin during acute COVID (COVID-OUT) also reduced later LC, per the Solving ME/CFS treatments summary. Together this suggests the early acute phase may be a window for intervention, which fits the Dubbo finding that acute severity predicts later illness.

studies.result: nirmatrelvir associated with reduced PCC risk

contradicting.result: no reduction in PCC with nirmatrelvir or molnupiravir

open_questions: Would early antivirals for EBV (e.g., during IM) prevent post-IM ME/CFS? No trial exists.

findings.finding: In a 30-patient RCT of 6 months of valganciclovir in CFS patients selected for high HHV-6 and EBV IgG, the primary MFI-20 outcome was not significant, though some secondary fatigue and cognitive trajectories favoured the drug.
findings.plain: A strong antiviral helped some tiredness and thinking measures in a small trial, but missed its main goal. It has never been repeated, and it can lower white blood cell counts.
findings.detail: Montoya 2013 (J Med Virol): 2:1 randomisation. The MFI-20 difference at 9 months was non-significant. Trajectories for MFI-20 mental fatigue (p=0.039), FSS (p=0.006) and cognition (p=0.025) were significant, and responder status was 7.4x more likely (p=0.029). Monocytes fell and neutrophils rose. These came from multiple secondary endpoints with no multiplicity correction. Preceding uncontrolled data: Kogelnik 2006 (n=12, 9 responders) and Watt 2012 chart review (n=61, 52% responders, baseline titres did not predict response). Lerner's valacyclovir 'EBV subset' series had small controlled phases and are largely uncontrolled. Antibody titre selection is a weak marker of active infection.

studies.result: primary MFI-20 ns; secondary FSS, mental fatigue, cognition significant
52% responders; titres did not predict response
Energy Index improved more on valacyclovir

open_questions: No adequately powered replication in 13 years
Would selection on lytic markers (plasma DNA, dUTPase, EA-D) rather than IgG identify responders?

findings.finding: Human endogenous retrovirus (HERV) expression in blood cells differs between ME/CFS, fibromyalgia and controls in small studies (HERV-K raised in moderate ME/CFS; HERV microarray profiles clustered n=43 participants perfectly by diagnosis).
findings.plain: Old viral DNA built into our genome can switch back on. Small studies hint that its activity pattern differs in ME/CFS, but nothing is confirmed.
findings.detail: Rodrigues 2019: qPCR found HERV-K overexpressed only in moderately affected patients, with no HERV-W difference. Giménez-Orenga 2025 (eLife; HERV-V3 microarrays, >350k HERV elements, PBMC, n=43 women): hierarchical clustering separated ME/CFS, FM, co-diagnosed and controls 'perfectly'. That sample is very small with very many features, so overfitting is likely without an independent validation set. HERV-K dUTPase antibodies co-occur with herpesvirus dUTPase antibodies in the Ariza lab data (Palomo 2026). Herpesviruses such as EBV can transactivate HERVs, which links this to the herpes hypothesis.

studies.result: HERV-K up in moderate ME/CFS; HERV-W no difference
HERV profiles clustered ME/CFS, FM, both and HC separately

open_questions: Replication in an independent, larger, blinded cohort
Are HERV proteins (Env) present in tissues or serum?

findings.finding: Temelimab, an antibody against HERV-W envelope protein, did not reduce fatigue versus placebo in a 203-person RCT of HERV-W-positive post-COVID patients.
findings.plain: A drug designed to block an endogenous retrovirus protein was tested in long COVID patients who had that protein, and it worked no better than placebo.
findings.detail: Nehme 2026 (Brain Behav Immun; GeNeuro-funded, NCT05497089): 24 weeks of monthly IV 54 mg/kg in participants selected for HERV-W ENV positivity. The PROMIS fatigue change was -3.2 vs -3.8 points, with no secondary benefit. Note that temelimab targets HERV-W, not HERV-K, so it does not test the HERV-K findings in ME/CFS. No temelimab trial in non-COVID ME/CFS exists.

studies.result: no difference in fatigue at 24 weeks

open_questions: Is HERV-K (rather than HERV-W) a better target in ME/CFS?

findings.finding: The 2009 report of the mouse retrovirus XMRV in 67% of CFS patients was a laboratory contamination artefact: blinded multi-lab and original-investigator studies found no XMRV/pMLV, and the Science paper was retracted.
findings.plain: In 2009 a mouse-derived virus was reported in most CFS patients. Careful blinded testing, including by the original scientists, showed it was contamination, and the paper was withdrawn.
findings.detail: Lombardi 2009 (Science) was partially retracted in 2011 and fully retracted later that year. Simmons 2011 (Blood XMRV Scientific Research Working Group): coded replicate samples sent to 9 labs, and reactivity was similar in CFS and controls. Alter 2012 (mBio; Lipkin-led, 147 CFS vs 146 controls, including the original investigators' labs) found no XMRV or pMLV. Lessons for this field: sensitive PCR contamination (mouse DNA in reagents and cell lines), unblinded testing, and premature clinical use (antiretrovirals were taken by some patients). The episode also set back trust and funding for virus research in ME/CFS.

studies.result: assays did not reproducibly detect XMRV/MLV; CFS = controls
no XMRV or pMLV in any group
contamination acknowledged in part of the data

findings.test_available: n/a (no valid XMRV test; commercial tests sold in 2010-11 were not meaningful)

findings.finding: In Finnish registry data, ME/CFS (G93.3) is enriched 3-6-fold for prior viral infections (HSV, EBV, influenza, COVID, viral CNS infection) but not for bacterial pneumonia or erysipelas.
findings.plain: In national health records, people with ME/CFS more often had earlier viral illnesses, but not more bacterial ones, which suggests viruses play a particular role.
findings.detail: Solving ME/CFS re-analysis of FinnGen R12 and FinRegistry (Risteys) found observed/expected ratios of 2-6 for viral infection codes vs ≤1 for bacterial codes, and protozoal intestinal infection was also enriched (18x). Limitations: FinnGen and FinRegistry overlap, so they are not independent. Coding and healthcare-seeking bias can inflate associations, and the timing of infection relative to onset is not always resolved. Infection-onset ME/CFS shares genetic risk with other onsets (DecodeME). The Giardia and Q fever outbreaks show that non-viral triggers also occur, so the viral excess is not absolute.

studies.cite: Solving ME/CFS re-analysis (epi_literature; FinnGen R12 / FinRegistry)
studies.result: viral infections O/E 3-6; bacterial pneumonia/erysipelas not enriched
raised risk after influenza

contradicting.result: bacterial pneumonia also raises ME/CFS risk (aHR about 1.4)

open_questions: Age/sex-matched time-to-event hazard ratios by infection class in UK Biobank or Danish registries

findings.finding: Unbiased blood virome/EV sequencing does not find more viruses in ME/CFS; a TTMV subgroup signal is unreplicated.
findings.plain: Searches of patients' blood for viruses find no excess, and sometimes fewer, than in controls.

studies.result: fewer viruses in patients
no enterovirus RNA

contradicting.result: TTMV9 in subgroup

hypotheses_notes.for: SARS-CoV-2 antigen/RNA persists in plasma and tissues of a minority for months to years, and tissue RNA associated with LC (Zuo 2024 OR 5.17). Enterovirus protein in stomach biopsies (Chia 2008). Early nirmatrelvir may prevent LC (small RCT).
hypotheses_notes.against: Three RCTs of nirmatrelvir in established LC (about 1,200 people) were null, and spike levels did not fall with treatment. Enterovirus findings are unreplicated with blinded methods. XMRV was contamination. The Giardia and Q fever triggers and failed doxycycline in QFS fit a 'hit-and-run' rather than persistent infection.

hypotheses_notes.for: Lytic-marker serology (EA-D) associates with LC fatigue (Peluso 2023). dUTPase antibodies higher in ME/CFS (one lab, repeated). HHV-6 miRNA in ME/CFS brain (n=3). Genetic EBV-load MR suggestive (MVP OR 1.59). Plasma EBV DNA more frequent in one study. Herpes titres track complement activation in LC.
hypotheses_notes.against: Large serology studies (UK Biobank, Swedish cohorts) show no difference. PBMC viral DNA is equally common. The valganciclovir RCT missed its primary outcome and was never replicated. MR signal is not EBV-specific on negative controls. Most positive findings come from single labs.

hypotheses_notes.for: HERV-K overexpression in moderate ME/CFS (Rodrigues 2019). HERV transcript profiles separate ME/CFS from FM (n=43). HERV-K dUTPase antibodies co-occur with herpes dUTPase antibodies. Definition: reactivation of human endogenous retroviral elements, possibly transactivated by herpesviruses, driving immune dysregulation.
hypotheses_notes.against: All studies are small and unreplicated. The anti-HERV-W antibody temelimab failed in HERV-W-positive post-COVID patients (n=203).

hypotheses_notes.for: Deficient EBV-specific memory B/T responses (Loebel 2014). Exhausted, terminally differentiated virus-specific CD8 T cells in LC (Ma 2026).
hypotheses_notes.against: Single-cell re-analysis found no exhausted CD8 signature in ME/CFS, and EBV-specific clonotypes trended higher, not lower, in severe cases.

hypotheses_notes.for: Classical complement activation associated with herpesvirus antibody titres in active LC (Cervia-Hasler 2024).
hypotheses_notes.against: Not yet replicated in non-COVID ME/CFS, and causal direction unknown.

hypotheses_notes.for: Severity of acute illness, not pathogen type, predicts post-infective fatigue (Dubbo). The stereotyped syndrome after diverse pathogens suggests a common host response.
hypotheses_notes.against: Few studies measure the acute immune response prospectively, and baseline cytokines have predicted outcome inconsistently.

hypotheses_notes.for: Stereotyped phenotype across pathogens, with no ongoing pathogen required (Dubbo, QFS doxycycline failure).
hypotheses_notes.against: Does not explain why only ~10% persist, or tissue-specific viral findings.

hypotheses_notes.for: Giardia outbreak produced lasting fatigue + IBS. SARS-CoV-2 gut persistence. Enterovirus in stomach (contested).
hypotheses_notes.against: Gut reservoir data are mostly in LC and convenience samples.

glossary.plain: A lasting illness of fatigue, pain, poor concentration and unrefreshing sleep that begins after a documented infection.
Herpesviruses hide quietly in cells for life (latent). When they 'wake up' and make new virus or viral proteins, that is lytic activity, or reactivation.
Parts of Epstein-Barr virus that antibodies are measured against. EA-D antibodies suggest recent reactivation, VCA IgM suggests a new infection, and EBNA IgG shows an old past infection.
An enzyme some herpesviruses make when partly reactivated. It can itself stir up inflammation, and antibodies to it are used as a sign of reactivation.
Inherited chromosomally integrated HHV-6: about 1 in 100 people carry HHV-6's genome in every cell, inherited from a parent. It can make blood HHV-6 tests look falsely 'high'.
A coat protein of enteroviruses (the family of polio, coxsackie and echoviruses) used to stain tissue for evidence of infection.
Viral protein detectable in the blood.
Human endogenous retroviruses: remnants of ancient viral infections that make up about 8% of our DNA and can sometimes be switched back on.
A mouse-derived retrovirus once reported in CFS. The finding was later shown to be lab contamination and retracted.
Using genetic variants as a natural experiment to test whether a trait (like EBV load) plausibly causes a disease.

key_reviews.why: Critical review of enterovirus methods in ME/CFS: why past studies neither proved nor excluded persistent infection.
Review of evidence for a SARS-CoV-2 tissue reservoir in long COVID and research priorities for antiviral trials.
The foundational prospective cohort showing a stereotyped post-infective syndrome across pathogens.
The definitive blinded study closing the XMRV episode, and a model for testing a pathogen claim.
Careful multiplex herpesvirus serology in Canada-criteria ME/CFS with a discussion of why serology is limited.

gaps: No adequately powered, replicated antiviral RCT in ME/CFS (valganciclovir n=30 in 2013 is still the best evidence).
No LC antiviral trial has enrolled people selected by biomarker evidence of persistence (antigenemia or tissue RNA).
No prospective trial of early antiviral treatment during infectious mononucleosis to prevent post-IM ME/CFS.
Blinded, multi-lab, sequencing-based tissue studies (gut, muscle, brain) for enterovirus, herpesvirus and SARS-CoV-2 in non-COVID ME/CFS are missing.
Longitudinal viral sampling timed to PEM crashes (plasma EBV/HHV-6 DNA, dUTPase, EA-D) has barely been done.
DecodeME iciHHV-6 prevalence results are not yet published.
Independent replication of dUTPase antibody findings outside the originating lab.
Whether post-COVID, post-EBV, post-Giardia and post-Q-fever ME/CFS share the same downstream biology.

domains.title: Metabolism and blood omics
domains.overview: Blood metabolomics and proteomics consistently find that ME/CFS patients differ from controls on average, but the differences are small (mostly 0.2-0.5 SD), partly cohort-specific, and confounded by medication, caffeine, diet and sample handling. The better-supported signals are modest: lower plasmalogens and some phosphatidylcholines, slightly lower carnitines, lower gut-derived IPA, lower aromatic lactates (a new cross-cohort re-analysis finding), higher methionine sulfoxide, and lower muscle-derived proteins in blood that are not explained by activity. Bigger claims, such as a uniform hypometabolic 'cell danger' state, an IDO metabolic trap, divergent metabolic or proteomic responses to exercise, reproducible methylation signatures, and diagnostic classifiers with near-perfect accuracy, have not held up in independent data or remain untested outside the original lab. No omics test is ready for diagnosis. The largest gaps are severe patients, sampling during the 48-72 h PEM window, disease controls, and pairing omics with fresh-cell function.

findings.finding: Blood metabolome differences between ME/CFS and controls are real at group level but small (mostly 0.2-0.5 SD) and partly cohort-specific; early near-perfect classification did not carry over to new cohorts.
findings.plain: Patients' blood chemistry differs from healthy people's on average, but only slightly, and the specific list of chemicals changes from study to study.
findings.detail: Single-cohort studies reported AUCs of 0.82-0.96 (Naviaux 2016, Nagy-Szakal 2018, Che 2022), but these were estimated within the training data. A harmonised re-analysis of 10 public cohorts found 74 compounds at q<0.05 with pooled effects mostly 0.2-0.5 SD; two Cornell cohorts agreed only weakly (rho 0.16) and cross-cohort transfer AUCs were 0.56-0.83. Medication exposure (paracetamol, gabapentin, psychoactives, acid suppressants detected in blood) and caffeine are major confounders that most original papers did not adjust for.

studies.result: 20 pathways abnormal; 80% of discriminating metabolites lower; AUC 0.94 (men, 8 metabolites) and 0.96 (women, 13) within the same data

studies.design: case-control, untargeted plasma metabolomics + stool metagenomics
studies.result: altered choline, carnitine and complex lipids; ceramide higher in the ME/CFS+IBS subgroup; cross-validated AUC 0.82 (metabolome), 0.84 combined with stool
lower plasmalogens/ether phospholipids, phosphatidylcholines and sphingomyelins (p<0.001); higher dicarboxylic acids; ML AUC up to 0.873

studies.design: harmonised meta-analysis of public per-person data (Metabolon, Fiehn, LC-MS/MS, NMR)
studies.result: 74 compounds q<0.05; effects mostly 0.2-0.5 SD; panel trained on BioMapAI transfers with AUC 0.60-0.83

contradicting.result: patient-control differences agree only faintly (rho 0.16); model trained on one scores AUC 0.56 on the other; a public GitHub copy of Germain 2020 has case/control labels swapped

contradicting.design: deep neural net on stool metagenome, plasma metabolome, immune profiling, labs, symptoms
contradicting.result: 10-fold CV AUC 0.915 (all omics); external cohorts AUC 0.59-0.77 (Guo, Raijmakers stool; Germain metabolome 0.68, Che 0.61) with 19-79% feature overlap

open_questions: Which differences persist in drug-free, fasting, rapidly processed samples?
Does any metabolite change track severity or PEM within a person?

findings.finding: Naviaux 2016's picture of a homogeneous 'hypometabolic' dauer-like state (80% of discriminating metabolites decreased) has not been confirmed as a uniform pattern in later independent cohorts.
findings.plain: One influential 2016 study said patients' cells were in a protective 'low-power' mode, with most chemicals reduced. Later studies found more mixed and smaller changes.
findings.detail: Naviaux's 45/39 cohort with targeted LC-MS/MS found lower sphingolipids, phospholipids, purines and other pathways and proposed the cell danger response (CDR). An Open Medicine Foundation validation cohort was reported informally (2018) to reproduce 23 of 30 pathway abnormalities, but no peer-reviewed replication paper was found. Hoel 2021 found heterogeneous metabotypes rather than one state; Che 2022 and Xiong 2023 partly echo the lipid reductions. In the cross-cohort re-analysis, the Naviaux data still carry some replicated signals (e.g. low aromatic lactates on a non-Metabolon platform), but there is no global hypometabolic shift across cohorts.

studies.result: 20 pathways abnormal; 80% of discriminating metabolites lower; AUC 0.94 (men, 8 metabolites) and 0.96 (women, 13) within the same data
23/30 pathway abnormalities reported as replicated

contradicting.result: common changes consistent with energy strain and altered fatty-acid/amino-acid fuel use; 3 patient subsets (metabotypes), 2 with distinct energy-metabolism patterns

contradicting.design: harmonised meta-analysis of public per-person data (Metabolon, Fiehn, LC-MS/MS, NMR)
contradicting.result: 74 compounds q<0.05; effects mostly 0.2-0.5 SD; panel trained on BioMapAI transfers with AUC 0.60-0.83

open_questions: Has the OMF validation cohort been published with per-person data?
Is any CDR signature (e.g. purinergic signalling) measurable in tissue rather than plasma?

findings.finding: Lower plasmalogens, some phosphatidylcholines and sphingomyelins are reported across several cohorts and platforms, with modest effect sizes.
findings.plain: Some fats that form cell membranes, especially a type called plasmalogens, are a little lower in patients' blood in several studies.
findings.detail: Che 2022 (106/91) reported lower plasmalogens/ether phospholipids, PCs and sphingomyelins (p<0.001) and proposed peroxisomal dysfunction. Naviaux 2016 found lower sphingolipids; Xiong 2023 lower sphingomyelins; Nagy-Szakal 2018 higher ceramides only in the IBS subgroup. In the cross-cohort re-analysis PC(14:0/16:0) was -0.42 SD (4 cohorts, 3 non-Metabolon) and plasmalogen P-16:0/18:2 -0.38 SD; dihydroceramide d18:0/16:0 was +0.28. Diet (dairy, fish) and BMI are not well controlled.

studies.result: lower plasmalogens/ether phospholipids, phosphatidylcholines and sphingomyelins (p<0.001); higher dicarboxylic acids; ML AUC up to 0.873
20 pathways abnormal; 80% of discriminating metabolites lower; AUC 0.94 (men, 8 metabolites) and 0.96 (women, 13) within the same data
plasma butyrate, bile acids, benzoate lower; sphingomyelins depleted; dysbiosis mostly in short-term patients
PC(14:0/16:0) -0.42 SD; plasmalogen P-16:0/18:2 -0.38 SD; dihydroceramide +0.28 SD

contradicting.design: case-control, untargeted plasma metabolomics + stool metagenomics
contradicting.result: altered choline, carnitine and complex lipids; ceramide higher in the ME/CFS+IBS subgroup; cross-validated AUC 0.82 (metabolome), 0.84 combined with stool

open_questions: Are plasmalogens low in tissue (muscle, red cells) or only plasma?
Do they relate to peroxisomal enzyme activity or to diet?
findings.test_available: research only (plasmalogen panels exist in some specialist labs)

findings.finding: Four aromatic 2-hydroxy acids (phenyllactate, 4-hydroxyphenyllactate, indolelactate, imidazole lactate) are lower in ME/CFS in 5 of 5 cohorts (combined -0.53 SD, I²=0), robust to drug, caffeine, diet and kidney-function adjustment.
findings.plain: A family of small chemicals made from amino acids is consistently lower in patients across five separate studies. It is a group-level difference, not a test.
findings.detail: Solving ME/CFS re-analysis: p=4e-11, holds on Naviaux's targeted LC-MS/MS platform (-0.64), -0.64 in people with no prescription drug detected, -0.73 in men. The precursor keto acids are not lower, so either the reduction step or a dietary source (fermented foods) is implicated. In BioMapAI paired stool, gut species do not predict these compounds (CV R²≈0), unlike IPA. They do not track severity (|r|<0.2). Not yet reported by original study authors; needs targeted, fasting confirmation and D- vs L-isomer separation (bacterial D vs host L).

studies.result: combined -0.53 SD, 5/5 cohorts lower, I²=0; not stool-predicted; not severity-linked

open_questions: Is this host lactate-dehydrogenase-type reduction, renal handling, or fermented-food intake?
D- vs L-phenyllactate ratio?
Does it differ from other fatigue conditions?

findings.finding: Indole-3-propionate (IPA), a gut-bacterial tryptophan product, is lower in ME/CFS plasma in 4 of 4 cohorts (-0.33 SD) and tracks butyrate-producing gut species.
findings.plain: A chemical made only by certain gut bacteria is a bit lower in patients, which fits the gut-bacteria differences found in several studies.
findings.detail: Pooled -0.33 SD (95% CI -0.49 to -0.16), p=0.0001; individual AUC only 0.57-0.60. In BioMapAI paired stool, IPA correlates with F. prausnitzii and Bifidobacterium and inversely with R. gnavus; adjusting for IPA-linked species reduces the difference from -0.40 to -0.09 (optimistic same-data selection). Xiong 2023 and BioMapAI report reduced microbial butyrate and altered tryptophan metabolism. Interpreted as a gut-ecology marker rather than a host defect.

studies.design: deep neural net on stool metagenome, plasma metabolome, immune profiling, labs, symptoms
studies.result: 10-fold CV AUC 0.915 (all omics); external cohorts AUC 0.59-0.77 (Guo, Raijmakers stool; Germain metabolome 0.68, Che 0.61) with 19-79% feature overlap
plasma butyrate, bile acids, benzoate lower; sphingomyelins depleted; dysbiosis mostly in short-term patients

open_questions: Does raising IPA (fibre, polyphenols) change anything clinically?
Is low IPA a consequence of diet changes caused by illness?

findings.finding: The IDO metabolic-trap model predicts tryptophan-kynurenine pathway disruption, but blood data are inconsistent: one cohort found higher kynurenine, others found no difference or slightly lower kynurenine.
findings.plain: A mathematical theory proposed that a tryptophan-processing enzyme gets stuck in ME/CFS. Blood measurements of that pathway point in different directions in different studies.
findings.detail: Kashi, Davis and Phair 2019 modelled IDO1 substrate inhibition plus common non-functional IDO2 variants producing a bistable 'trap'; it is a hypothesis paper with no patient data. Kavyani 2024 reported higher kynurenine correlating with severity and lower downstream 3-HK, 3-HAA, QUIN, picolinate. Groven 2021 (49 CFS/57 FM/54 HC women) found differences mainly in FM, not CFS vs controls. The cross-cohort re-analysis found kynurenine -0.27 SD (lower), kyn/trp ratio -0.19 (q=0.06), lower kynurenine with >4 years illness, and no change in IDO1/KYNU proteins. Plasma kynurenine says little about intracellular IDO kinetics, which is what the model is about.

studies.result: IDO1 substrate inhibition + IDO2 loss + LAT1 asymmetry gives two steady states

studies.design: case-control, plasma KP metabolites + cytokines + proteomics
studies.result: higher kynurenine linked to severity; lower 3-HK, 3-HAA, QUIN, PIC; hepcidin about halved

contradicting.result: main differences FM vs HC; quinolinic acid differs CFS vs FM; no clear CFS vs HC kynurenine shift

contradicting.design: harmonised meta-analysis of public per-person data (Metabolon, Fiehn, LC-MS/MS, NMR)
contradicting.result: kynurenine -0.27 SD (lower); kyn/trp -0.19, q=0.06; lower in >4 y illness; IDO1/KYNU protein null
3-hydroxyanthranilic acid and 3-hydroxykynurenine differ; no headline kynurenine rise

open_questions: Do IDO2 variants differ in frequency in large genetic data (DecodeME)?
Intracellular tryptophan/kynurenine flux in patient cells under stress?
findings.test_available: Plasma tryptophan/kynurenine available in some commercial labs; not diagnostic

findings.finding: Free carnitine and long-chain acylcarnitines are slightly lower in ME/CFS across cohorts, contrary to the earlier idea of excess circulating fatty acids.
findings.plain: Carriers that move fats into the cell's power stations are a little lower in patients' blood.
findings.detail: Reported as altered/low in Naviaux 2016, Nagy-Szakal 2018, Germain 2017 and Germain 2022 (carnitines low). Cross-cohort re-analysis: carnitine -0.21 SD, long-chain acylcarnitines -0.22 SD, long-chain fatty acids slightly lower in all 4 cohorts examined; acetylcarnitine/carnitine ratio null. Germain 2020 reported lower acyl cholines. Effect sizes are small and diet/fasting status is rarely recorded.

studies.design: case-control, untargeted plasma metabolomics + stool metagenomics
studies.result: altered choline, carnitine and complex lipids; ceramide higher in the ME/CFS+IBS subgroup; cross-validated AUC 0.82 (metabolome), 0.84 combined with stool
74/361 metabolites p<0.05, 35 at q<0.15; fatty-acid and lipid pathways
acyl cholines lower in two cohorts; steroid changes
carnitine -0.21 SD; long-chain acylcarnitines -0.22 SD
lower acetylcarnitine / altered acylcarnitines

contradicting.result: hypothesis of higher fatty acids in patients reversed: long-chain fatty acids and acylcarnitines slightly lower

open_questions: Muscle carnitine and fatty-acid oxidation flux in vivo?
Effect of fasting and dietary restriction on these values?
findings.test_available: Plasma acylcarnitine profile (clinical metabolic labs); not diagnostic for ME/CFS

findings.finding: Several studies infer impaired carbohydrate oxidation (pyruvate dehydrogenase restraint, TCA/urea cycle shifts), but simple blood ratios (lactate/pyruvate, citrulline/arginine) do not differ across pooled cohorts.
findings.plain: Some studies suggest patients' cells burn sugar less efficiently. Blood measures that should show this are mostly normal when many studies are pooled.
findings.detail: Fluge 2016 (200/102) found low TCA-fuelling amino acids in women and higher PDK1/2/4 mRNA in PBMCs; Hoel 2021 described energy strain with altered fuel use in subsets; Yamano 2016 found TCA/urea-cycle ratios (validation AUC 0.75). Armstrong 2015 (NMR, 34/25 women) reported lower blood lactate and glutamate and higher glucose. In the pooled re-analysis, lactate/pyruvate (-0.10), citrulline/arginine, ornithine/arginine and hypoxanthine/xanthine were null; creatine/creatinine +0.19. These are inferences from plasma about tissue metabolism; direct tissue flux measurements are scarce.

studies.design: case-control, serum amino acids + PBMC mRNA
studies.result: lower TCA-fuelling amino acids mainly in women; PDK1/2/4, SIRT4, PPARδ mRNA higher; suggests impaired pyruvate dehydrogenase
common changes consistent with energy strain and altered fatty-acid/amino-acid fuel use; 3 patient subsets (metabotypes), 2 with distinct energy-metabolism patterns
TCA and urea-cycle intermediates differ; ornithine/citrulline + pyruvate/isocitrate AUC 0.80 train, 0.75 validation
lower lactate, acetate, glutamate; higher glucose (via review table)

contradicting.result: lactate/pyruvate, NO/urea-cycle and purine ratios null; no support for an arginine/NO substrate problem

open_questions: Does PDH activity measured in muscle biopsies differ?
Are Hoel's metabotypes stable over time in the same person?

findings.finding: Ketone bodies are associated with ME/CFS in UK Biobank NMR data, but 3-hydroxybutyrate shows no consistent difference in pooled case-control cohorts.
findings.plain: One very large data set links ketones (fuel made from fat) to ME/CFS; smaller studies pooled together do not.
findings.detail: Huang 2024 (1,194 ME/CFS in UK Biobank, NMR) reported lipoprotein and ketone-body associations; their ML model (19 baseline characteristics + 9 NMR biomarkers) reached AUC 0.83, with much of the signal from non-omic features. Fasting time and diet differ by group and strongly affect ketones. Pooled re-analysis: 3-hydroxybutyrate null; ketones used as a covariate did not explain other signals.

studies.design: UK Biobank NMR metabolomics, association + ML
studies.result: 168 biomarker associations incl. surface lipids and ketone bodies; AUC 0.83 with 19 baseline characteristics + 9 NMR markers

contradicting.result: 3-hydroxybutyrate null

open_questions: Ketones under controlled fasting with orthostatic measures?

findings.finding: Germain 2022 reported growing metabolic divergence after a 2-day CPET; within-person re-analysis finds the exercise response itself barely differs (blunted lactate and glucose rise aside).
findings.plain: A study took blood before and after two exercise tests and saw bigger differences after. Re-analysed person by person, the changes caused by exercise look mostly the same in patients and controls.
findings.detail: Germain 2022 (60/45, 1,157 metabolites, 4 time points) found female significant counts rising from 6 to 54 across time points. Re-analysis: day-1 and day-2 case-control differences correlate 0.85 and are only ~6% larger on day 2; within-person change scores are at chance (permutation p=0.12-0.61). Surviving signals: smaller lactate rise (likely lower workload), no post-exercise glucose rise in patients, oxidised cys-gly rising only in patients. Five of 8 people with missing post-exercise samples were severely affected men.

studies.result: baseline differences; authors report growing patient-control divergence after exercise in lipid and energy pathways

contradicting.result: exercise response at chance; 3 modest signals; no reproducible response subgroups (ARI 0.01)

open_questions: Samples at 48-72 h, when PEM peaks?
Workload-matched comparisons?

findings.finding: Collagen breakdown products (hydroxyproline, galactosyl-hydroxylysine and related) are higher in ME/CFS plasma (+0.52 SD, 4/4 Metabolon cohorts; hydroxyproline also up on 3 other platforms).
findings.plain: Fragments released when collagen (the body's connective-tissue protein) is broken down are a bit higher in patients.
findings.detail: Solving ME/CFS re-analysis only: p=2e-8 for the module; hydroxyproline +0.31 SD across 8 cohorts. Galactosyl-hydroxylysine weakens after drug adjustment. Collagen/gelatin supplements and diet are not excluded. Fits loosely with lower ECM/fibroblast and vascular mural proteins in the proteome re-analysis, but the direction (more breakdown, less matrix protein) needs direct markers (CTX-I, PIIINP).

studies.result: collagen module +0.52 SD; hydroxyproline +0.31 SD

open_questions: Link to hypermobility / POTS subgroups?
Supplement and diet history?

findings.finding: Markers of oxidative stress (methionine sulfoxide, oxidised glutathione products, lower brain glutathione) are repeatedly reported, but they are non-specific and also seen in depression.
findings.plain: Signs that cells are under chemical 'rust' stress show up in several studies, but the same signs appear in other illnesses too.
findings.detail: Methionine sulfoxide/methionine +0.35 SD in 7/7 cohorts across 3 platforms (I²=0), though methionine oxidises during storage; 5-oxoproline/glutamate -0.25 SD (Solving ME/CFS re-analysis). Germain 2018 proposed broad redox imbalance; Germain 2022 data show oxidised cys-gly rising after exercise in patients only. Shungu 2012 (MRS, 15 CFS/15 MDD/13 HC) found lower cortical glutathione and higher ventricular lactate in both CFS and depression. Antioxidant trials have not shown clear benefit.

studies.result: 14 metabolites differ; authors propose broad redox imbalance
higher ventricular lactate, lower cortical glutathione in CFS and MDD; no CFS-MDD difference in GSH
methionine sulfoxide ratio +0.35 SD, I²=0
Lymphocytes from 27 ME/CFS and 20 LC showed raised oxidative stress, higher glutathione, lower SOD2 and lipid oxidative damage, with sex differences; metformin damped T-cell hyperproliferation
exaggerated oxidative stress after exercise
muscle oxidative damage

open_questions: Does MetSO hold in rapidly processed samples with matched storage time?
Is oxidative stress cause, consequence, or shared with any chronic illness?

findings.finding: NAD+ depletion is a proposed mechanism but has not been directly established in ME/CFS cohorts; NAD precursor trials raise NAD+ without clear clinical benefit.
findings.plain: NAD+ is a molecule cells need for energy. The idea that patients lack it is mostly theory; supplements raise it but have not clearly helped.
findings.detail: Reviews (Dehhaghi 2022) link the kynurenine pathway to NAD+ synthesis. Castro-Marrero 2015 (n=73) and 2021 (n=207) RCTs of CoQ10 200 mg + NADH 20 mg reported modest improvements in some fatigue/cognitive scores. A long-COVID RCT of nicotinamide riboside 2 g/day (n=58) raised blood NAD+ 2.6-3.1x but showed no between-group difference in cognition or fatigue (p=0.59), with high dropout. Vitamin B3 pathway changes appeared in Abujrais 2024 untargeted data.

studies.result: links KP hyperactivation and NAD+ metabolism in ME/CFS
reduction in cognitive fatigue and some QoL measures reported
fatigue impact score reduced; PBMC NAD+/NADH, ATP higher

contradicting.result: NAD+ up 2.6-3.1x; no difference in cognition, fatigue, sleep

open_questions: Is intracellular NAD+/NADH measurably low in patient muscle or immune cells?
findings.test_available: research only (some commercial NAD+ tests exist but are not validated for ME/CFS)

findings.subdomain: Proteomics and blood traits: UK Biobank
findings.finding: In UK Biobank, ME/CFS cases show many small blood-trait differences (inflammation, insulin resistance, liver markers) that replicate partly in All of Us and are not explained by low physical activity.
findings.plain: In a huge UK database, people with an ME/CFS diagnosis have many slightly different blood results, and this is not just because they move less.
findings.detail: Beentjes, Ponting and colleagues used semi-parametric (Super Learner, one-step) estimators with activity, walking pace and other mediators. 9 of 14 tested traits replicated in All of Us; people reporting PEM showed stronger differences. Caveats: diagnosis is from records/self-report, so case definition is loose; UK Biobank skews healthier and older; differences are small and single traits do not separate groups. Olink proteomics summary statistics show LEP, ADH4, BCHE, complement factors up and CA14, SOD3 down (Solving ME/CFS re-analysis).

studies.n: up to 1,455 cases vs 131,303 controls (UK Biobank); All of Us replication
studies.design: population cohort, 3,237 blood traits, mediation analysis
studies.result: hundreds of traits differ (116 in both sexes): inflammation, insulin resistance, liver; 9/14 replicated in All of Us; activity mediates only 1/3,237; no single trait discriminates
Metabolite GWAS, 875 ME/CFS vs 36,033 controls: ME/CFS-specific SNPs at HSD11B1 and SCGN for lipoprotein lipids; lipid pathway enrichment

open_questions: Do these survive stricter case definitions (e.g. DecodeME-style questionnaires)?
How much reflects BMI, medication and comorbidity?
findings.test_available: Routine labs (CRP, HbA1c, liver enzymes) exist but are not diagnostic

findings.finding: Muscle-derived intracellular proteins (myoglobin, troponins, CA3 and similar) are lower in resting ME/CFS blood across three SomaScan cohorts and UK Biobank Olink, and this is not explained by activity measures.
findings.plain: Proteins that normally leak from muscle into blood are a little lower in patients, perhaps meaning less muscle or slower muscle turnover, not ongoing muscle damage.
findings.detail: Hoel 2026 reported reduced intracellular skeletal-muscle proteins. Solving ME/CFS re-analysis: muscle theme d -0.50 (95% CI -0.76 to -0.24), q=0.002, I² 0.07 across Hoel (-0.85), Germain (-0.43), Walitt (-0.34); UKB competitive shift negative; not mediated by walking pace, not related to steps, Bell score or time reclined. Lean mass was not measured, so reduced muscle mass remains a plausible explanation.

studies.result: 1,823 aptamers differ (845 FDR); secreted proteins up, intracellular (skeletal muscle) proteins down; lower activated-neutrophil secretion
muscle_damage set d -0.50, q=0.002

open_questions: Does it survive adjustment for DXA lean mass?
Relation to muscle biopsy fibre size and capillarisation?
findings.test_available: CK and myoglobin are routine but expected low-normal; not diagnostic

findings.finding: Most of the ~845 FDR-significant serum proteins in Hoel 2026 appear driven by a sample-handling (cell-leak) signal that is absent from other cohorts; about 13 survive adjustment.
findings.plain: A large protein study found hundreds of differences, but a re-analysis suggests most came from how samples were handled rather than the illness.
findings.detail: Solving ME/CFS re-analysis built a nuclear/cell-leak score: case-control d -1.16 in Hoel, ~0 in Germain, Walitt serum and Walitt CSF. After adjustment Hoel keeps 13 FDR hits (COMP, C6, ANTXR2, LAMA2, FAP and others). Hoel's raw statistics correlate with Germain only through intracellular proteins, and not after adjustment. Hoel authors validated a selection by antibody methods. Across ~6,000 proteins meta-analysed in 4 cohorts, only 32 reach q<0.05 and replicated effects are d 0.25-0.5 (ITGAV, NOTCH3, THBS1, LUM, ADH4, GSTA1, BAFF up).

studies.result: 1,823 aptamers differ (845 FDR); secreted proteins up, intracellular (skeletal muscle) proteins down; lower activated-neutrophil secretion

contradicting.result: leak score separates only Hoel (d -1.16); 13 hits survive

open_questions: Were case and control samples processed with different delays?
Do the 13 surviving proteins replicate prospectively?

findings.finding: Hepatocyte enzymes (ADH4, GSTA1, AGXT, BCHE) are modestly higher, and vascular mural/matrix proteins (ITGAV, NOTCH3, LUM, THBS1, TGF-beta family) modestly lower, in more than one cohort.
findings.plain: A few groups of blood proteins, from the liver and from the walls of small vessels, are slightly shifted in several data sets.
findings.detail: Liver set d +0.40 (q=0.013) but defined after seeing data and tracks BMI; up in Germain and UKB, partly Hoel, not in long COVID. Mural/ECM: ITGAV -0.34 (4 cohorts), NOTCH3 -0.32, TGF-beta set -0.44 (q=0.013); a long COVID UK Olink set also shows lower ECM/endothelial proteins. Endothelial 'activation' markers go down, not up, and platelet/microclot proteins are not raised. Expected candidates (renin, ACE, endothelin, BNP, EPO, hepcidin, NEFL, GFAP, IL-6, CRP) are null.

studies.result: liver +0.40; TGF-beta -0.44; ITGAV -0.34; many named candidates null

studies.n: up to 1,455 cases vs 131,303 controls (UK Biobank); All of Us replication
studies.design: population cohort, 3,237 blood traits, mediation analysis
studies.result: hundreds of traits differ (116 in both sexes): inflammation, insulin resistance, liver; 9/14 replicated in All of Us; activity mediates only 1/3,237; no single trait discriminates

open_questions: Do liver proteins survive adjustment for fatty-liver index and ALT/GGT?
Do lower NOTCH3/ITGAV reflect pericyte loss or shedding?
findings.test_available: Routine liver tests; otherwise research only

findings.finding: Germain 2025 reported patient-specific proteomic changes during recovery after a 2-day CPET, but a within-person re-analysis of the same data finds no protein whose exercise response differs at FDR.
findings.plain: One large study reported that patients' blood proteins react differently to exercise. When re-analysed person by person, no single protein clearly did.
findings.detail: Germain 2025: 79 ME/CFS vs 53 sedentary controls, 6,361 proteins, 2 CPETs 24 h apart; pathway-level claims of suppressed T/B-cell and IL-17 signalling and raised glycolysis. Re-analysis: 0 FDR hits for differential change; no tissue score changes with exertion. Smaller EV studies after CPET (Giloteaux 2024, 18/17 women; Glass 2025, 10/12 men) report altered EV cargo responses (TCA down, complement up at 15 min; ER-stress proteins correlating with PEM), but n is small.

studies.result: widespread changes after exertion, most in recovery; suppressed T/B signalling and IL-17, higher glycolysis proteins; sex differences

studies.design: CPET, EV TMT proteomics, 3 time points
studies.result: EV proteome response differs; changes correlate with severity
TCA proteins down, complement up 15 min post-exercise; ER-stress changes track PEM

contradicting.result: 0 FDR hits for differential exercise response

open_questions: Sampling at 48-72 h?
Effort-matched comparison and correction for lower workload?

findings.finding: Plasma extracellular vesicle (EV) counts may be higher in ME/CFS, but no EV protein or microRNA difference has survived multiple-testing correction in a replicated cohort.
findings.plain: Tiny particles cells release into blood may be more numerous in patients, but their contents have not shown a reliable difference yet.
findings.detail: Rydland 2026 (49/50, SEC + MS proteomics): higher EV concentration; 11 of 424 proteins differ nominally (erythroid, hepatocyte, plasma-cell origin), none after FDR. Re-analysis of Rydland and Giloteaux EV data: no FDR hits. Eguchi 2026 EV-miRNA study had 6 ME/CFS. EV isolation methods vary widely and platelet activation during handling changes EV counts.

studies.result: more EVs; 11 nominal protein differences, none FDR
candidate EV-miRNAs; very small n
Plasma EV cargo altered (haemoglobin alpha, IGFALS); let-7b-5p lower in post-COVID ME/CFS (12 vs 15) and tracked symptoms; small n
Higher plasma EV counts in ME/CFS and LC-ME/CFS than recovered controls (FDR-significant); more leukocyte, monocyte and platelet EVs, fewer B-cell EVs

contradicting.result: no FDR hits

open_questions: Standardised EV isolation across sites?
Do EV counts change with PEM?

findings.finding: CSF proteomics in ME/CFS is limited to small cohorts and has not produced a replicated protein difference; the largest recent study (31 patients) had no controls.
findings.plain: Studies of the fluid around the brain and spine are few and small, and have not found a consistent difference.
findings.detail: Bragee 2026 (31 patients, 902 proteins): within-patient associations with POTS (neutrophil degranulation, platelet activation) and severity (complement, coagulation, IGFBP); re-analysis found 0 FDR hits POTS vs no-POTS. Walitt 2024 CSF SomaScan (~17 vs 21) showed no FDR hits in re-analysis, and no rise in neuronal injury markers. Earlier CSF proteome reports (Schutzer 2011, Baraniuk 2005) were small.

studies.result: POTS- and severity-associated pathways; hypothesis-generating

studies.design: CFS vs neurologic post-Lyme vs controls, CSF MS
studies.result: distinct CSF proteomes reported

contradicting.result: 0 FDR hits; NEFL/GFAP null

open_questions: Adequately powered CSF study with controls and severe patients?

findings.finding: Blood transcriptome and single-cell RNA studies report monocyte and platelet abnormalities, but no gene or cell subtype difference replicates across independent cohorts.
findings.plain: Studies reading which genes are switched on in blood cells found possible differences, but they have not repeated in other groups of patients.
findings.detail: Vu 2024 (scRNA, ~30/28, before and 24 h after CPET) reported classical monocyte dysregulation correlating with severity and platelet activation signatures post-exercise. Re-analysis of the same data at person-level pseudobulk: 0 genes at q<0.05 at baseline in 15 cell types; composition null. Across 4 bulk RNA cohorts, 0 genome-wide FDR genes; a plasma-cell/immunoglobulin score is lower in 2/4 (meta d -0.42, p=0.06). Higher mitochondrial RNA fraction in lymphocytes (CD8 Tem d +0.85) is a lead that did not replicate in bulk PBMC. Walitt 2024 reported sex-specific PBMC expression differences in 17/21 people.

studies.result: monocyte dysregulation tracking severity; platelet activation post-exercise

studies.design: deep phenotyping incl. PBMC RNA, flow, metabolomics
studies.result: sex-specific gene expression and metabolic differences; fewer switched-memory B cells

contradicting.result: no replicated gene or cell-type difference

open_questions: An independent PBMC scRNA cohort (only one lab has published so far)?
Severe and housebound patients?

findings.finding: Reported genome-wide blood DNA methylation differences have not replicated across cohorts, at least one large set is explained by cell-composition differences, and epigenetic clocks are not accelerated.
findings.plain: Chemical tags on DNA were reported to differ in patients, but a closer look shows the differences mostly reflect which blood cells were in the sample.
findings.detail: de Vega 2014/2017/2018, Trivedi 2018 (13/12 discovery, 17,296 CpGs; pyrosequencing in 33/31) and Helliwell 2020 (RRBS, 10/10) each reported many differentially methylated sites with little overlap. Re-analysis of 4 cohorts (177/107): in GSE93266, control 'PBMC' DNA contained much more granulocyte DNA (median 48% vs 14%); 44,794 FDR CpGs fall to 0 after composition adjustment; meta-analysis 0 CpGs at q<0.05. Horvath, Hannum, PhenoAge, GrimAge, DunedinPACE null in T cells and saliva. Commercial epigenetic-age tests are not supported for ME/CFS.

studies.result: 17,296 CpGs in 6,368 genes; 307 promoters
76 fragments, 394 CpGs; overlap with earlier gene lists
differential methylation in immune genes
PBMC methylation, n=5 per group: 214 differentially methylated fragments in ME/CFS and 429 in LC, 118 shared; very small study
Methylation changed over 0, 24 and 48 h after two-day CPET in 5 patients, unlike 2 controls; very small study

contradicting.result: 0 replicated CpGs; clocks normal

open_questions: Sorted-cell methylation in a large, age-matched cohort?
findings.test_available: research only (consumer epigenetic-age tests are not validated here)

findings.finding: A nanoelectronic impedance assay separated 20 ME/CFS from 20 controls perfectly after hyperosmotic stress, but there is no published independent replication.
findings.plain: A chip measuring how blood cells react to salt stress separated a small group of patients from controls completely. Nobody outside the lab has confirmed it.
findings.detail: Esfandyarpour 2019 (PNAS) used PBMCs incubated in plasma; patients' impedance rose after NaCl stress, controls' did not; plasma swap suggested a plasma factor. The only independent attempt found was a 4 vs 4 bioimpedance preprint (Fernandez 2023) with a different device, which reported higher impedance at one frequency and did not test the original protocol. No disease-control group (e.g. MS, depression) was reported in the original at scale; device-to-device variability is unaddressed in published work.

studies.result: complete separation after hyperosmotic stress; plasma swap effect

contradicting.result: higher impedance at 1.36 kHz; not a replication of the original protocol

open_questions: Blinded multi-site validation with disease controls?
What molecule in plasma drives the effect?

findings.finding: Raman spectroscopy of PBMCs or plasma separates ME/CFS from controls in single-centre studies (plasma AUC 0.83-0.85), without external validation.
findings.plain: A laser technique that reads the chemical 'fingerprint' of blood looked promising in two labs, but has not been tested in new patients elsewhere.
findings.detail: Xu 2019 (single-cell Raman, PBMCs) found higher phenylalanine-associated bands in patients, similar to mtDNA-depleted rho0 cells; small n. Heidarifard 2026 (115 ME vs 45 sedentary controls, plasma at rest and 90 min after a standardised stress) reported AUC 0.85 and 0.83, specificity 73% and 69%. Models are trained and tested within one cohort; spectral features are hard to map to specific molecules.

studies.result: higher phenylalanine bands in CFS PBMCs

studies.design: plasma Raman + ML, rest and post-stress
studies.result: AUC 0.85 (rest), 0.83 (post-stress)

open_questions: Independent external test set and disease controls?

findings.finding: Plasma cell-free RNA classified ME/CFS vs sedentary controls with test-set AUC 0.81 and suggested platelet, pDC and monocyte-derived differences; not yet externally validated.
findings.plain: RNA fragments floating in blood plasma could tell patients from controls about 4 times in 5 in one study.
findings.detail: Gardella 2025 (PNAS; 93 vs 75 sedentary controls): LASSO model, held-out test AUC 0.81, accuracy 77%; deconvolution suggested differences in platelet-derived cfRNA and higher pDC, monocyte and T-cell cfRNA; network analysis pointed to cytokine signalling and T-cell exhaustion. Held-out test within one cohort; the plasma-cell score that dips in PBMC data was null in this cfRNA set in re-analysis.

studies.result: test AUC 0.81; platelet, pDC, monocyte cfRNA differences

open_questions: Performance in a second cohort and against fibromyalgia, depression, long COVID?

findings.finding: Multi-omic machine-learning classifiers (BioMapAI and others) perform well in cross-validation but drop to AUC ~0.6-0.77 on external cohorts, so none is usable for diagnosis.
findings.plain: Computer models trained on many blood and stool measurements do well on the data they learned from but much worse on new patients.
findings.detail: BioMapAI (Xiong 2025, 249 participants, 4-year longitudinal sampling) reached 10-fold CV AUC 0.915 with all omics; on external cohorts AUC was 0.72 and 0.59 (Guo stool), 0.61-0.77 (Raijmakers), 0.68 (Germain metabolome) and 0.61 (Che), with only 19-79% feature overlap. Repeated visits per person raise the question of whether CV folds were split by person; disease controls were not included. A small metabolite panel derived in the Solving ME/CFS re-analysis transferred with AUC 0.60-0.83. Huang 2024 UK Biobank AUC 0.83 relied heavily on 19 baseline (non-omic) characteristics. No multi-omic layer converges on a shared pathway beyond chance (re-analysis).

studies.design: deep neural net on stool metagenome, plasma metabolome, immune profiling, labs, symptoms
studies.result: 10-fold CV AUC 0.915 (all omics); external cohorts AUC 0.59-0.77 (Guo, Raijmakers stool; Germain metabolome 0.68, Che 0.61) with 19-79% feature overlap
AUC 0.83, recall 0.70
20 pathways abnormal; 80% of discriminating metabolites lower; AUC 0.94 (men, 8 metabolites) and 0.96 (women, 13) within the same data

contradicting.result: patient-control differences agree only faintly (rho 0.16); model trained on one scores AUC 0.56 on the other; a public GitHub copy of Germain 2020 has case/control labels swapped
no protein-RNA-metabolite-genetics convergence beyond chance (one modest protein-metabolite rho 0.28)

open_questions: Pre-registered external validation with disease controls (fibromyalgia, depression, MS, long COVID)?
Person-level train/test splits for longitudinal data?

findings.finding: Even the deepest blood omics studies sample mainly at rest, in mild-to-moderate patients, in plasma or serum only, and rarely test fresh-cell function or the 48-72 h PEM window.
findings.plain: The biggest blood studies so far mostly leave out the sickest patients, the days when symptoms flare after effort, and live-cell tests.
findings.detail: Walitt 2024 (NIH, 17/21) is the deepest per person but tiny and excluded many severe patients by design. BioMapAI has 4 years of visits but resting samples only. Germain 2022/2025 and Giloteaux/Glass cover 0, 15 min and 24 h after CPET but not 48-72 h, and the most impaired cannot do CPET (5 of 8 missing post-exercise samples were severe men). UK Biobank is large but one baseline time point with loose case definition. Hoel 2021/2026 are resting serum. Fresh-cell assays (PBMC respiration, NK function, red-cell deformability) are rarely paired with omics; compartments like muscle, CSF and gut tissue are rarely sampled together.

studies.result: many layers measured, small n

studies.design: deep neural net on stool metagenome, plasma metabolome, immune profiling, labs, symptoms
studies.result: 10-fold CV AUC 0.915 (all omics); external cohorts AUC 0.59-0.77 (Guo, Raijmakers stool; Germain metabolome 0.68, Che 0.61) with 19-79% feature overlap
widespread changes after exertion, most in recovery; suppressed T/B signalling and IL-17, higher glycolysis proteins; sex differences

studies.n: up to 1,455 cases vs 131,303 controls (UK Biobank); All of Us replication
studies.design: population cohort, 3,237 blood traits, mediation analysis
studies.result: hundreds of traits differ (116 in both sexes): inflammation, insulin resistance, liver; 9/14 replicated in All of Us; activity mediates only 1/3,237; no single trait discriminates

open_questions: Who will run a multi-omic study in severe/housebound patients with home sampling?
Dense sampling through a PEM episode?

findings.finding: Haptoglobin and FGF-21 have been proposed as blood markers of PEM-related biology in single-centre studies with validation cohorts.
findings.plain: Two blood proteins track with post-exertional symptoms in early studies.

studies.result: haptoglobin associated with ME/CFS/PEM
FGF-21 elevated

findings.finding: Shorter leukocyte telomeres in CFS, driven by women under 45, in a population-based sample.
findings.plain: One large study found shorter chromosome caps (telomeres), a marker of cell ageing.

studies.result: shorter telomeres in CFS, mainly younger women

findings.finding: Low circulating serotonin in long COVID (attributed to viral RNA persistence, interferon and reduced tryptophan uptake) has not reproduced in a later cohort.
findings.plain: A high-profile study found low serotonin in long COVID; a follow-up did not.

studies.result: serotonin reduced in LC; linked to viral persistence/IFN

contradicting.result: no reduction
methodological concerns

hypotheses_notes.for: Naviaux 2016: 80% of discriminating metabolites lower; lipid/purine changes; Hoel 2021 energy strain.
hypotheses_notes.against: No peer-reviewed replication of a homogeneous hypometabolic profile; pooled cohorts show small, mixed shifts.

hypotheses_notes.for: Fluge 2016 PDH pattern; lower carnitines/acylcarnitines; low muscle proteins in blood; Germain 2022 blunted glucose rise; Hoel 2021 metabotypes.
hypotheses_notes.against: Lactate/pyruvate and other energy ratios null in pooled data; exercise metabolome response mostly normal within person.

hypotheses_notes.for: Model plausibility (Kashi 2019); Kavyani 2024 higher kynurenine tracking severity.
hypotheses_notes.against: Pooled data show slightly lower kynurenine; kyn/trp ratio null; IDO1/KYNU protein null; plasma cannot test intracellular kinetics.

hypotheses_notes.for: Low IPA in 4/4 cohorts tied to butyrate producers; Xiong 2023 low plasma butyrate; BioMapAI connectivity.
hypotheses_notes.against: Aromatic lactates, the strongest metabolite signal, are not stool-predicted.

hypotheses_notes.for: Methionine sulfoxide +0.35 SD in 7/7 cohorts; Germain 2018; post-exercise oxidised cys-gly; Shungu 2012 low brain GSH.
hypotheses_notes.against: Same changes in depression; storage artefacts possible; antioxidant trials unconvincing.

hypotheses_notes.for: Higher collagen breakdown products; lower ECM/fibroblast and mural proteins.
hypotheses_notes.against: Re-analysis only; diet/supplements not excluded.

hypotheses_notes.for: Lower NOTCH3, ITGAV, TGF-beta and vascular smooth-muscle protein sets.
hypotheses_notes.against: Endothelial activation and platelet/microclot protein sets are lower, not higher.

hypotheses_notes.for: cfRNA T-cell exhaustion signature (Gardella 2025); Germain 2025 suppressed T/B signalling after exertion; plasma-cell RNA dip.
hypotheses_notes.against: No replicated single-cell or bulk transcript difference.

hypotheses_notes.for: Nanoneedle plasma-swap effect; Fluge 2016 serum effects on myoblasts.
hypotheses_notes.against: No independent replication of the nanoneedle assay.

hypotheses_notes.for: Complement up in Hoel and UKB; EV complement rise post-exercise in men.
hypotheses_notes.against: Complement direction inconsistent across cohorts (down in Walitt); platelet set lower.

glossary.plain: Measuring hundreds to thousands of small molecules (sugars, fats, amino acids, drug traces) in a sample at once.
Measuring thousands of proteins at once; SomaScan uses DNA-like aptamers, Olink uses antibody pairs. Both can be distorted by how a sample is handled.
How far apart the group averages are, in units of normal person-to-person spread. 0.2 is small, 0.5 moderate, 0.8 large.
How well a test separates two groups: 0.5 is a coin flip, 1.0 is perfect. Values from the same data used to build a model are usually too optimistic.
Naviaux's idea that cells under threat switch into a protective, low-energy mode, which in ME/CFS fails to switch off.
A model in which the tryptophan-processing enzyme IDO1 gets stuck in a low-activity state because of substrate inhibition and inactive IDO2 variants.
Membrane fats made partly in peroxisomes; thought to protect against oxidation.
Fats bound to carnitine for transport into mitochondria; their profile hints at how fat is burned.
Tiny membrane bubbles released by cells into blood, carrying proteins and RNA.
RNA fragments in plasma released by dying or active cells, showing which tissues are busy.
Chemical tags on DNA that change gene activity; clocks estimate biological age from them. Results depend heavily on the mix of cell types.
Testing a model on parts of the same data set vs on a completely separate group of people. Only the second shows real-world performance.

key_reviews.why: Overview of metabolite biomarker studies in ME/CFS and animal models.
Review of lipid, energy and oxidative-stress omics across ME/CFS, Gulf War illness and fibromyalgia.
Review of the kynurenine pathway case in ME/CFS.
Largest blood-trait analysis, with explicit handling of inactivity as a confounder.
Largest longitudinal multi-omic data set; reports external validation numbers worth reading critically.

gaps: No multi-omic study in severe or housebound patients with home sampling.
No dense sampling across a PEM episode (48-72 h and beyond); exertion studies stop at 24 h.
Very few studies include disease controls (fibromyalgia, depression, MS, deconditioning, long COVID) needed to test specificity.
Drug exposure, caffeine, fasting status and sample processing time are rarely recorded or adjusted, despite large effects on metabolomics and proteomics.
No pre-registered, multi-site external validation of any diagnostic classifier (nanoneedle, Raman, cfRNA, BioMapAI).
Targeted confirmation of low aromatic lactates (with D/L isomers) and high collagen breakdown in fasting, drug-free samples.
Lean mass not measured alongside the low muscle-protein signal.
Fresh-cell functional assays (PBMC respiration, NK cytotoxicity, red-cell deformability) are not paired with omics in the same people.
Only one lab's PBMC single-cell RNA data exist; no independent scRNA cohort.
Intracellular NAD+/NADH and tryptophan flux have not been measured directly in patient tissue.

comprehensive_studies.name: Walitt 2024 (NIH intramural)
comprehensive_studies.compartments: plasma, CSF, PBMC, stool, muscle physiology, brain imaging
comprehensive_studies.limits: very small n; results by sex underpowered

comprehensive_studies.name: BioMapAI / Xiong 2025 (JAX, Bateman Horne)
comprehensive_studies.compartments: plasma metabolome, stool metagenome, immune flow, routine labs
comprehensive_studies.timepoints: up to 4 yearly visits at rest

comprehensive_studies.name: Germain 2022 / 2025, Giloteaux 2024, Glass 2025 (Cornell)
comprehensive_studies.n: 60/45 metabolome; 79/53 proteome; EV subsets 18/17 F, 10/12 M
comprehensive_studies.timepoints: pre/post CPET day 1 and day 2 (15 min, 24 h)
comprehensive_studies.limits: no 48-72 h samples; most impaired excluded or missing

comprehensive_studies.name: Hoel 2021 / Hoel 2026 (Bergen)
comprehensive_studies.limits: sample-handling signal in proteome; per-person data not public

domains.title: Hormones
domains.overview: The most consistent hormone finding in ME/CFS is a mildly under-active stress-hormone (HPA) axis: on average cortisol is slightly low in saliva, urine and hair, and feedback suppression is exaggerated. A 2026 meta-analysis of 46 case-control studies confirms this pattern. The shifts are small, most patients fall inside normal reference ranges, and they may be a consequence of illness, sleep disruption or inactivity rather than a cause. Low-dose hydrocortisone gave at best a small, short-lived benefit with side effects, and fludrocortisone failed in two large trials. Newer leads concern the hormones that hold water and salt in the body: low vasopressin and a 'renin-aldosterone paradox' that would fit the low blood volume seen in many patients. These come from small or uncontrolled studies, and the vasopressin finding is not matched by copeptin, which is the more reliable test. The female preponderance (about 1.5 to 3 times more women) is solid, but genetics shows no sex-specific risk variants, and the role of sex hormones, menopause and gynaecological conditions is still only descriptive.

findings.finding: On average, people with ME/CFS have mildly lower free cortisol (salivary awakening and morning cortisol, 24-h urinary cortisol and hair cortisol) than healthy controls.
findings.plain: Cortisol is the body's main stress and energy-mobilising hormone. On average it runs a little low in ME/CFS, but the gap is modest and most individual results are still normal.
findings.detail: Woo et al. 2026 pooled 46 case-control datasets (1,388 patients, 1,349 controls, 71.9% female) and found lower salivary awakening and morning cortisol, 24-h urinary free cortisol and hair cortisol. Hair cortisol, which reflects about 3 months of exposure, was also lower in a small adolescent study (Vroegindeweij 2024). In the Solving ME/CFS literature tally, 19 groups report lower cortisol and 5 higher. In untargeted plasma metabolomics the signal is weak and inconsistent: Germain 2020 −0.64 SD, Germain 2022 −0.13, BioMapAI −0.05, with men −0.35 (Solving ME/CFS re-analysis). The meta-analysis does not separate cause from effect: sleep disruption, inactivity, illness duration and antidepressant use can all lower cortisol.

studies.result: Lower salivary awakening/morning, 24-h urinary and hair cortisol

studies.n: 12 ME/CFS, 20 Q-fever fatigue, 8 post-COVID, 19 JIA vs 57 controls
studies.result: Lower hair cortisol in fatigued patients than controls
19 lower vs 5 higher cortisol
low cortisol

contradicting.cite: Solving ME/CFS re-analysis of BioMapAI plasma metabolome
contradicting.result: Plasma cortisol −0.05 SD overall (men −0.35, p=0.04)
null after FDR

open_questions: Is low cortisol present at onset, or does it develop with illness duration and inactivity?
Does cortisol track PEM or severity within a person over time?
How much do medication, sleep timing and sampling time explain?
