studies.result: No difference in COMPASS-31 (p=0.629)
Benefit reported
Case series, 17 infection-related ME/CFS on low-dose subcutaneous IgG for 5 weeks: improved symptoms and quality of life; uncontrolled
improvement

contradicting.result: No benefit over placebo
No benefit

open_questions: What will RECOVER-AUTONOMIC's IVIG arm show?
Is there a small-fibre-neuropathy subgroup that responds?
findings.test_available: Prescribed in some specialist clinics; costly

findings.finding: Rintatolimod (Ampligen) gave a modest placebo-adjusted gain in treadmill time in a 234-person phase III trial, but the result was borderline and the FDA declined approval.
findings.plain: An immune-stimulating drug given by drip twice a week helped exercise time a little in one large company trial; regulators did not find this convincing.
findings.detail: AMP-516 (Strayer 2012): 40 weeks IV 400 mg twice weekly; intention-to-treat placebo-adjusted exercise tolerance +21.3% (p=0.047), +28% after compliance correction; reduced use of symptomatic drugs (p=0.048). Lead authors employed by the manufacturer. FDA issued a complete response letter in 2009 and has not approved it. A 2020 post hoc analysis suggested better response in illness of 2-8 years' duration. Not replicated by an independent group.

studies.result: Exercise tolerance +21.3% vs placebo (p=0.047)

contradicting.result: Benefit concentrated in 2-8 years' duration (hypothesis-generating)

open_questions: Would an independent trial with a pre-specified duration subgroup replicate?
findings.test_available: Expanded access in the US only

findings.finding: The anti-HERV-W envelope antibody temelimab did not improve fatigue versus placebo in 203 HERV-W-positive long-COVID patients.
findings.plain: A drug aimed at a dormant virus-like gene product that can be switched on after infection did not help long-COVID fatigue in a proper trial.
findings.detail: GNC-501 (GeNeuro, 2024): IV temelimab vs placebo, primary endpoint 3-point fall in PROMIS Fatigue SF-7a at week 24; no clinically meaningful difference and most secondary endpoints negative; well tolerated. Company suggested shorter disease duration or changes in HERV-W status may matter (post hoc). Company press release; full peer-reviewed paper not seen.

studies.result: Primary fatigue endpoint not met

open_questions: Is HERV-W activation a marker without causal role?

findings.finding: Low-dose rapamycin (6 mg weekly) was followed by self-reported improvement in about three-quarters of completers in an uncontrolled decentralised study; randomised trials are pending.
findings.plain: A low weekly dose of an immune-modulating drug thought to restart cellular clean-up (autophagy) was followed by improvement in many patients, but no one in the study got a placebo.
findings.detail: Ruan 2025: 86 enrolled, 70 reached day 30; 52 (74.3%) reported improvement in fatigue, PEM and orthostatic intolerance, with MFI and SF-36 gains; autophagy markers (pSer258-ATG13 down, BECLIN-1 up) moved and correlated with outcomes. No serious adverse events. Follow-on metabolomics (Gile 2026) in responders only. Uncontrolled response rates of this size are similar to placebo responses in RCTs (35-40%+) plus attrition bias. The Mount Sinai placebo-controlled trial in long COVID (NCT06960928, ~80-90) ends Nov 2026.

studies.result: 74.3% improved; autophagy markers changed
Purine metabolism and mitochondrial changes in responders

open_questions: Will the Mount Sinai RCT confirm benefit?
Can autophagy markers select responders prospectively?
findings.test_available: Off-label prescription in some US clinics; research only in UK

findings.finding: Three randomised trials of nirmatrelvir-ritonavir (Paxlovid) for 15-25 days in established long COVID (total ~1,200 people) found no benefit on any phenotype.
findings.plain: If leftover coronavirus were driving long COVID, an antiviral might help. Three good trials found it did not, at least at the doses and durations tested.
findings.detail: RECOVER-VITAL (Baden 2026): 959 randomised to 15 or 25 days vs placebo-ritonavir, cognitive, autonomic and exercise phenotypes; no primary benefit (e.g. autonomic -6.4%, 95% CI -18.5 to 5.7). STOP-PASC (Stanford, n=155, 15 days) and PAX LC (Yale, n=100, 15 days, PROMIS-29) also null. STOP-PASC immune profiling found no EBV reactivation or microclot differences versus controls. The trials do not exclude a role for persistence in tissue reservoirs that this drug fails to reach, or effects in very early or highly selected patients.

studies.result: No benefit for any phenotype at day 90
No change in PROMIS-29 physical score vs placebo
No benefit

open_questions: Would longer courses, combination antivirals or monoclonal antibodies (trials under way) reach tissue reservoirs?
Is there a biomarker of persistent antigen that would select responders?

findings.finding: Valganciclovir in 30 patients selected for high HHV-6 and EBV antibody levels improved some secondary fatigue and cognition scores in a small RCT; it has not been replicated.
findings.plain: Antivirals against herpesviruses have been tried in patients with high antibody levels, with modest results in one small trial. High antibodies show past infection, not necessarily active virus.
findings.detail: Montoya 2013: 2:1 randomised, 6 months; reported benefit on MFI mental fatigue (p=0.039), Fatigue Severity Scale (p=0.006) and cognition (p=0.025); primary endpoint detail not confirmed this session. Preceded by an open-label series (Kogelnik 2006, 9/12 near-resolution). Neutropenia risk requires monitoring. Lerner's valacyclovir/valganciclovir EBV-subset series are uncontrolled. Selection by IgG titre is a weak marker of active replication.

studies.result: Secondary fatigue/cognition improvements
9/12 near resolution

open_questions: Would selection by viral DNA (PCR) rather than antibody titre identify responders?
findings.test_available: EBV/CMV/HHV-6 PCR and serology are clinically available; antiviral use off-label

findings.finding: The first sizeable placebo-controlled trial of low-dose naltrexone in post-COVID ME/CFS (66 vs 71, 16 weeks, up to 4.5 mg) found no fatigue benefit, with over 40% improving on placebo.
findings.plain: Low-dose naltrexone is widely used off-label and many patients report benefit. In a proper trial, the drug did not reduce fatigue more than placebo. Pain and subgroup results are still being analysed.
findings.detail: The trial is Canadian (Nacul, University of British Columbia; NCT05430152), presented at the Berlin International ME/CFS Conference, May 2026; preliminary and unpublished. Earlier evidence was retrospective (Polo 2019, n=218, 74% self-reported benefit) or uncontrolled long-COVID series. The LIFT trial (pyridostigmine x LDN factorial, n=160, Harvard/OMF, NCT06366724) and a RECOVER paediatric trial are pending. Effects on pain, sleep or specific subgroups remain possible.

studies.cite: Nacul et al., presented May 2026 (UBC; NCT05430152)
studies.result: Primary (fatigue) not met; >40% placebo responders
no benefit of LDN
reported benefit (uncontrolled)

contradicting.result: 74% reported benefit

open_questions: Does LDN help pain or a pain-predominant subgroup?
What will the LIFT factorial show?

findings.finding: In a retrospective single-clinic review, 74% of 101 patients on very low-dose aripiprazole (mostly 0.25-2 mg) reported improvement; there is no randomised trial.
findings.plain: A tiny dose of an antipsychotic drug, thought to act on dopamine and brain immune cells, was linked to improvement in a clinic's records, but this kind of study cannot rule out placebo or selective reporting.
findings.detail: Crosby 2021 (Stanford): 101 patients; ~74% reported improvement in brain fog, fatigue, unrefreshing sleep or energy; side effects included insomnia, akathisia, vivid dreams. Retrospective, no control, outcomes from clinic notes. Rationale (microglial modulation, dopamine partial agonism) is speculative. No RCT reported as of Oct 2026.

studies.result: 74% improved

open_questions: Would a placebo-controlled trial confirm benefit?

findings.finding: A single 60 mg pyridostigmine dose raised peak oxygen uptake relative to placebo on a repeat invasive exercise test in 45 ME/CFS patients with preload failure, largely because the placebo group got worse; longer trials are negative or pending.
findings.plain: Pyridostigmine boosts nerve signalling that tightens veins and returns blood to the heart. In a one-day lab study it stopped exercise capacity dropping on a second test. Whether it helps daily life is untested; the factorial LIFT trial should answer that.
findings.detail: Joseph/Systrom 2022: 23 vs 22; peak VO2 +13.3 vs -40.2 mL/min (difference ~54 mL/min), with cardiac output and right atrial pressure maintained instead of falling; oxygen extraction unchanged. Same-day laboratory endpoint. São Paulo 2025 (ATS abstract, long COVID with RV preload dysfunction, n=32, up to 360 mg/day for 6-10 weeks): negative overall (p=0.35), borderline +103 mL in a post hoc subgroup. Kanjwal 2011 POTS retrospective (n=203): 43% improved, 19% stopped for GI effects. LIFT (n=160, 13 weeks, FUNCAP-55 and CPET endpoints) has not reported.

studies.design: single-dose double-blind RCT between two iCPETs
studies.result: Peak VO2 +13 vs -40 mL/min
grip effect

contradicting.result: Negative overall (p=0.35)
43% improved; 19% stopped for GI effects

open_questions: Does LIFT show benefit on daily function?
Does preload failure on iCPET predict response?
findings.test_available: Licensed drug (myasthenia); off-label use; iCPET research only

findings.finding: Ivabradine lowered standing heart rate but did not improve symptoms in 181 people with long-COVID POTS (RECOVER-AUTONOMIC), despite an earlier positive 22-person crossover in hyperadrenergic POTS.
findings.plain: Slowing a racing heart is not the same as making people feel better. A large trial in long-COVID POTS showed exactly that.
findings.detail: Taub 2021: 22 hyperadrenergic POTS (noradrenaline >600 pg/mL), 1-month crossover; lower HR and better RAND-36 QoL. RECOVER-AUTONOMIC (2026, ACC late-breaker): 181 adults, 12 weeks; no meaningful change in orthostatic intolerance or long-COVID symptoms vs placebo, though supine-to-standing HR change fell significantly. The factorial coordinated non-pharmacological care arm (diet-mediated volume expansion, rehab, education) is reported separately. Full paper pending. Whether a hyperadrenergic subgroup benefits remains open.

studies.result: Lower HR and better QoL
No symptom benefit; HR change reduced

open_questions: Does a noradrenaline-defined hyperadrenergic subgroup respond?

findings.finding: Fludrocortisone did not beat placebo in a 100-person RCT in CFS with neurally mediated hypotension; midodrine reduces orthostatic heart rate acutely in small POTS studies but has no ME/CFS outcome trial.
findings.plain: Two standard drugs for low blood pressure on standing have been tried. Fludrocortisone, which makes the body hold salt, did not help in a proper trial in CFS. Midodrine tightens blood vessels and helps some POTS patients in the short term, but it has not been properly tested in ME/CFS.
findings.detail: Rowe 2001: fludrocortisone 0.1 mg vs placebo for 9 weeks in CFS + NMH on tilt; >=15-point wellness improvement in 14% vs 10% (p=0.76). Peterson 1998 (n=25) also negative. Midodrine: small acute crossover studies in POTS/orthostatic intolerance show lower standing HR (memory, not re-checked); risks include supine hypertension (relevant for bedbound patients). No ME/CFS RCT with function as endpoint. Grade refers to fludrocortisone; midodrine evidence is early.

studies.result: 14% vs 10% improved (p=0.76)

contradicting.cite: Ross 2014, Am J Physiol (midodrine in POTS)
contradicting.result: Improved orthostatic tolerance acutely

open_questions: Would a midodrine trial in ME/CFS with low-flow physiology show functional benefit?
findings.test_available: Licensed drugs; tilt test available on NHS

findings.finding: Two Spanish RCTs of CoQ10 200 mg + NADH 20 mg (n=73, n=207) reported modest reductions in fatigue scores; CoQ10 alone failed in a 121-person long-COVID crossover trial.
findings.plain: Supplements meant to support mitochondria produced small improvements in two trials from one group, with supplier involvement. CoQ10 on its own did nothing in long COVID.
findings.detail: Castro-Marrero 2015: 8 weeks, n=73; FIS-40 improved (p<0.05) with higher NAD+/NADH, CoQ10, ATP in PBMCs. Castro-Marrero 2021: 12 weeks, 104 vs 103; cognitive fatigue and FIS-40 total improved (p~0.02), SF-36 improved. Same research group, industry links; effect sizes small and not replicated independently. Hansen 2023 (Denmark, CoQ10 500 mg/day, n=121 crossover) in long COVID: no benefit.

studies.result: FIS-40 improved (p<0.05)
Cognitive fatigue and FIS-40 improved

contradicting.result: CoQ10 alone: no benefit

open_questions: Would an independent group replicate the CoQ10+NADH result?

findings.finding: Oxaloacetate 2 g/day reduced Chalder fatigue more than control (−25% vs −10%) in an 82-person company-run RCT in ME/CFS; a 69-person long-COVID trial missed its primary endpoint.
findings.plain: A supplement that feeds a step in energy metabolism reduced fatigue in one trial run with the manufacturer. A similar trial in long COVID did not meet its main goal.
findings.detail: RESTORE ME (Cash 2024): 90 days, 2,000 mg vs rice-flour control; fatigue −25% vs −10% (between-group p=0.0039); secondary analysis (Vernon 2025) showed cognitive gains at day 60. Sponsor (Terra Biological) involvement. REGAIN (long COVID, n=69, 42 days): primary Chalder negative, secondary cognition gains. No independent replication.

studies.result: Cognitive improvement at day 60 (p=0.034)

contradicting.result: Primary endpoint not met

open_questions: Independent replication with objective endpoints (actigraphy)?

findings.finding: Forty daily sessions of hyperbaric oxygen at 2.0 ATA improved cognition and symptoms versus sham in a 73-person long-COVID trial, but ten sessions at 2.4 bar showed no benefit in an 80-person sham-controlled trial.
findings.plain: Breathing pure oxygen under pressure helped in an Israeli trial with 40 sessions, but not in a Swedish trial with 10 sessions. Dose may matter, or the positive trial may not hold up. It needs daily travel, which many patients cannot do.
findings.detail: Zilberman-Itskovich 2022 (Tel Aviv): 37 vs 36, 40 sessions, 5/week, 100% O2 at 2.0 ATA for 90 min with air breaks, sham at 1.03 ATA air; global cognition improved (d≈0.5, p=0.038), plus energy, sleep, psychiatric symptoms and pain; benefits persisted at ~1-year follow-up in 31 patients (Hadanny 2024); a cardiac substudy showed improved GLS. HOT-LoCO (Kjellberg 2025, Sweden): 40 vs 40, 10 sessions over 6 weeks, 100% O2 at 2.4 bar 90 min vs air at 1.2-1.34 bar; RAND-36 PF difference 0.63 (95% CI −7.0 to 8.3, p=0.87); both groups improved. Charité (Kedor, 2026 conference): 20 vs 40 sessions; improvements only in the 40-session group (no sham arm reported). The 'sham' pressure differs between trials and blinding of pressure is imperfect. No ME/CFS (non-COVID) RCT.

studies.design: double-blind sham RCT, 40 sessions at 2.0 ATA
studies.result: Cognition, energy, sleep, pain improved
Improvements maintained
Open-label, 30 patients, 40 HBOT sessions: SF-36 physical function improved (g=0.71); no control arm

contradicting.design: double-blind sham RCT, 10 sessions at 2.4 bar
contradicting.result: No difference (RAND-36 PF diff 0.63, p=0.87)

open_questions: Is there a dose-response (sessions x pressure) in a single trial with proper sham?
Does it apply to non-COVID ME/CFS?
findings.test_available: Private clinics; not NHS-funded for this use

findings.finding: PACE (n=641) reported modest gains in self-rated fatigue and function with CBT and graded exercise, but these were not matched by objective measures, used Oxford criteria, and vanished between groups by 2.5 years.
findings.plain: The largest trial of talking therapy and gradually increasing exercise said both helped moderately. Re-analysis using the trial's own original plan found the benefits much smaller and limited to questionnaires that unblinded patients filled in.
findings.detail: White 2011: CBT and GET vs specialist medical care: Chalder fatigue −3.4 and −3.2 points, SF-36 PF +7.1 and +9.4 at 52 weeks; adaptive pacing no better than SMC. Long-term follow-up (Sharpe 2015): no between-group differences at median 31 months. Wilshire 2018 re-analysis using protocol-specified outcomes (data via FOI): CBT/GET did not significantly beat control after correction; recovery rates low (single digits to ~10%) and not different; objective measures (6-minute walk modest, step test, employment, benefits) largely null. Criticisms: Oxford criteria (fatigue only; PEM not required), outcome switching, unblinded self-report, mid-trial newsletter. Cochrane exercise review (Larun, re-dated 2024) rates evidence low-moderate and notes limited applicability to ME/CFS defined with PEM; a full update is pending.

studies.result: Modest self-reported gains for CBT/GET; APT no effect
No between-group differences at ~2.5 years

contradicting.result: CBT/GET not significantly better after correction; effects confined to self-report
Exercise may slightly reduce fatigue; low-certainty; applicability to PEM-defined ME/CFS uncertain

open_questions: Would a blinded-assessor trial with objective endpoints in PEM-defined patients show any benefit?

findings.finding: NICE's 2021 guideline (NG206) told clinicians not to offer graded exercise therapy, and patient surveys plus a 2026 German rehabilitation study report frequent worsening after exercise-based or even pacing-focused rehab.
findings.plain: England's health guidance body reviewed the evidence and concluded that the old exercise trials were low quality and that GET should not be offered. Large patient surveys and a German study suggest rehab programmes often make people worse.
findings.detail: NICE NG206 (Oct 2021): rated the GET/CBT evidence 'low' or 'very low' quality; recommends against GET or any programme based on fixed incremental increases; CBT may be offered only as supportive therapy, not as cure. Eckey/Xiao 2025 survey (n≈3,925): GET had a net score of about −72% (most harmful item). CFS_CARE (Charité, 2026 conference): a specialised rehab programme including pacing left 42 of 97 participants worse on the Bell scale, few better. Survey data are self-selected; CFS_CARE is uncontrolled and preliminary. Nevertheless the direction is consistent across sources.

studies.result: Do not offer GET; CBT only as supportive
GET net −72%
42/97 worsened

contradicting.result: No excess serious adverse reactions reported with GET

open_questions: What exactly distinguishes harmful from tolerable activity programmes?
How common is lasting deterioration after rehab in a controlled study?

findings.finding: Pacing (staying within one's energy limits) is the top-rated approach in patient surveys and NICE's recommended foundation, but it has never shown benefit in a controlled trial (adaptive pacing was no better than usual care in PACE).
findings.plain: Patients consistently rate pacing as the most helpful thing they do, and guidelines recommend it. It has not been properly tested in a trial designed with patients, so its benefit rests on consensus and self-report.
findings.detail: Eckey/Xiao 2025: pacing net score ~75% (highest of >150 treatments). PACE APT arm (n=160): no difference vs SMC. Critics argue APT in PACE was not the envelope-style pacing patients use. Pacing is plausible as harm avoidance (preventing PEM) rather than a treatment. Heart-rate-guided pacing studies are small and uncontrolled.

studies.result: Pacing net assessment ~75%

contradicting.result: APT no better than specialist care

open_questions: Does HR- or wearable-guided pacing reduce PEM frequency in a randomised trial?

findings.finding: A 3,925-person survey rated >150 treatments; illness severity predicted perceived response more strongly than diagnosis, and symptom clusters (severe multisystemic, POTS-dominant, cognitive/pain, mild) preferred different treatments.
findings.plain: Thousands of patients rated what helped. The cheap supportive measures came top (pacing, fluids, compression), graded exercise came bottom, and different kinds of patients reported benefit from different things.
findings.detail: Eckey, Li, Morrison, Davis, Xiao, PNAS 2025: ME/CFS and long COVID ratings correlated (R²=0.68). Top: pacing 75%, fluids/electrolytes ~69%, compression ~62%; GET −72%. Clusters: severe multisystemic (IVIG, lymphatic drainage), POTS-dominant (compression, autonomic modulators), cognitive (CNS stimulants), mild. Self-selected social-media sample, no placebo, recall bias; useful for prioritising trials, not for efficacy claims.

studies.result: Pacing, fluids, compression highest; GET lowest; severity shaped response

open_questions: Do survey-defined clusters map onto biological subgroups?

findings.finding: Placebo and natural-course improvement in ME/CFS and long-COVID trials is large (35% responders in RituxME, >40% in the LDN trial, both arms improving in IVIG, HBOT and immunoadsorption trials), so uncontrolled response rates of 50-75% are uninterpretable.
findings.plain: In almost every controlled trial, many people on the dummy treatment also improve. This is why open-label studies that report most patients getting better cannot show a treatment works.
findings.detail: RituxME placebo SF-36 PF 32.3 to 45.5 at 18 months; LDN >40% placebo responders; iSTAND albumin COMPASS −10.6; HOT-LoCO both arms improved; IAMPOCO both arms improved; BLOC failure attributed partly to placebo response. Contributing factors: regression to the mean (patients enrol when worse), natural fluctuation, expectation, and post-COVID spontaneous recovery in early cohorts.

studies.result: 35.1% placebo response
Albumin arm improved as much as IVIG
Both arms improved

open_questions: What run-in periods and objective endpoints best reduce placebo noise?

findings.finding: Full recovery from established adult ME/CFS is uncommon: a systematic review of 14 criteria-based cohorts found a median full-recovery rate of 5% (range 0-31%) and median improvement of 39.5%.
findings.plain: Most adults with long-standing ME/CFS do not fully recover, although many improve somewhat over years. Children and people early in the illness do better.
findings.detail: Cairns & Hotopf 2005: 28 studies, 14 with operational CFS criteria; full recovery median 5%, improvement 39.5% (8-63%); return to work 8-30%. Better outcome with lower baseline fatigue. Adolescents have better prognosis (studies report a majority improving or recovering over 5-10 years; memory, not re-checked). RituxME placebo arm at 6 years: 7.4% reached SF-36 PF >=90. Old cohorts used heterogeneous criteria; newer prospective data in post-COVID ME/CFS (Legler 2023) show little improvement to 20 months.

studies.result: Median full recovery 5%; improvement 39.5%
7.4% placebo at SF-36 PF >=90; 14.8% worsened >=20 points

open_questions: What are recovery rates in PEM-defined adult cohorts followed prospectively from onset?

findings.finding: About 4.5% of SARS-CoV-2-infected adults in RECOVER met IOM ME/CFS criteria (vs 0.6% uninfected; HR 4.93), and those meeting Canadian criteria at Charité stayed severely ill to 20 months while other long-COVID patients improved.
findings.plain: COVID roughly quintupled the rate of new ME/CFS. People whose long COVID meets ME/CFS criteria tend not to recover over the first two years, unlike milder long COVID.
findings.detail: Vernon 2025 (RECOVER-Adult, n=11,785 infected, 1,439 uninfected): incidence 2.66 vs 0.93 per 100 person-years; 88.7% of post-COVID ME/CFS also met long-COVID criteria; criteria based on self-report. Legler 2023 (Charité, n=106, 3-8, 9-16, 17-20 months): PCS-ME/CFS persistently severe; lower initial grip strength predicted persistence. Kedor 2022 (n=42): about half met CCC at 6 months.

studies.result: 4.5% vs 0.6% met ME/CFS criteria; HR 4.93
PCS-ME/CFS severity persistent at 20 months
~half met CCC ME/CFS at 6 months

open_questions: What fraction of post-COVID ME/CFS recovers by 5 years?

findings.subdomain: Natural history: prevalence and sex ratio
findings.finding: ME/CFS affects roughly 0.2-1% of adults depending on criteria (US 2021-22: 1.3% self-reported diagnosis; England: 0.16% with a hospital-recorded diagnosis), with women affected 3-4 times as often as men.
findings.plain: Somewhere between 1 in 100 and 1 in 500 adults have ME/CFS, depending on how it is counted. About three to four in every four patients are women.
findings.detail: Lim 2020 meta-analysis (46 studies): pooled prevalence 0.39%, meta-analytic 0.68% (0.48-0.97); women ~1.5-2x more often in pooled data. Vahratian 2023 (NHIS 2021-22): 1.3% of US adults (women ~1.7% vs men ~0.9%) — self-report of a clinician diagnosis plus current illness. UK: Nacul 2011 primary-care minimum 0.2%; Samms & Ponting 2025 (Hospital Episode Statistics): 100,055 diagnosed in England (0.16%), F:M 3.88:1, peaking ~6:1 in the 40s; white people ~5x more likely diagnosed, suggesting under-diagnosis. DecodeME's cohort is ~83% female. Commonly cited UK total: ~250,000-400,000 (estimate). Long COVID: ONS estimated ~2 million self-reported (~3%) in England/Scotland in 2024 (memory).

studies.result: Pooled 0.39%; meta-analytic 0.68%
1.3% of US adults
Minimum prevalence 0.2%
bimodal age/sex incidence

open_questions: Why the female predominance (DecodeME found few sex-specific loci)?
How much is under-diagnosis in men and ethnic minorities?

findings.finding: Roughly a quarter of people with ME/CFS are estimated to be housebound or bedbound, and severity, not diagnosis, was the strongest predictor of reported treatment response.
findings.plain: A large minority are too ill to leave home. Severely ill patients are under-represented in almost every trial, so trial results may not apply to them.
findings.detail: The 25% severe figure (often cited from IOM 2015 and UK charity surveys) rests on clinic and survey estimates, not population sampling (memory). Eckey/Xiao 2025: severity shaped treatment ratings more than ME/CFS vs long COVID. RituxME and CycloME excluded the most severe; Fluge's daratumumab study included moderate-to-severe. The original Fluge 2016 serum effect came from severe patients and the 2026 replication used mostly moderate patients.

studies.result: At least a quarter housebound/bedbound at some point (estimate)
Severity strongest correlate of response

open_questions: Population-based severity distribution?
Trials designed for severe, bedbound patients (home-based endpoints)?

findings.finding: In 2,147 secondary-care CFS patients in London, all-cause and cancer mortality were not raised, but suicide mortality was about seven times expected (SMR 6.85).
findings.plain: ME/CFS is not, on average, shown to shorten life in registry data, but suicide risk is markedly higher, and rare deaths from severe illness (for example malnutrition) are documented.
findings.detail: Roberts 2016 (SLaM CRIS, 2007-2013): 17 deaths; all-cause SMR 1.14 (0.65-1.85); cancer SMR 1.39 (0.60-2.73); suicide SMR 6.85 (2.22-15.98). Jason 2006 memorial-list analysis reported younger age at death from heart failure, cancer and suicide, but the sample is self-selected and biased. Deaths from severe ME with nutritional failure (e.g. UK coroner cases) are reported but not systematically counted. Small numbers of deaths limit precision.

studies.result: All-cause SMR 1.14 (NS); suicide SMR 6.85

contradicting.result: Younger mean age at death for several causes; biased sample

open_questions: Mortality in severe/very severe cohorts?
Suicide risk factors (disbelief, lack of care, pain)?

findings.finding: Clonidine did not improve activity or symptoms in adolescent CFS (NorCAPITAL RCT) and trended toward fewer steps, despite lowering noradrenaline and CRP.
findings.plain: A blood-pressure drug that calms the stress system did not help teenagers with CFS and may have reduced activity.

studies.result: steps -637/day vs placebo (p=.07); noradrenaline and CRP lowered; baseline higher noradrenaline and lower urinary cortisol

findings.finding: Fluoxetine did not improve fatigue in CFS in two RCTs.
findings.plain: An antidepressant (fluoxetine) did not help fatigue in two trials.
findings.detail: Subdomain label is a placeholder; propose new subdomain 'Neuro: antidepressants'.

studies.result: no effect on fatigue
no fatigue benefit from fluoxetine

findings.finding: Solriamfetol produced a fatigue benefit at week 8 but not at the primary 6-week point in a small RCT.
findings.plain: A wakefulness drug showed a small late benefit in one small trial.
findings.detail: Propose new subdomain 'Neuro: stimulants'.

studies.result: FSI improved at week 8 (p=.039), not week 6

findings.finding: IV saline produced short-term symptom relief in an open case series.
findings.plain: Salt-water drips helped short-term in an uncontrolled series.

studies.result: short-term improvement

findings.finding: Vitamin D supplementation in an open-label RCT in ME/CFS.
findings.plain: One unblinded vitamin D trial.

studies.result: modest symptom changes; unblinded

hypotheses_notes.for: Daratumumab 6/10 sustained responders with IgG fall (Fluge 2025); cyclophosphamide 55% open-label response; long-COVID IgG transfers pain-like symptoms to mice (Chen 2026).
hypotheses_notes.against: Rituximab phase III negative; immunoadsorption failed against sham twice; BC007 company trial negative; GPCR autoantibodies not elevated on REAP/Luminex (Germain 2025).

hypotheses_notes.for: Post-COVID ME/CFS incidence HR 4.93 (Vernon 2025); rintatolimod modest effect.
hypotheses_notes.against: Three nirmatrelvir RCTs null; temelimab null.

hypotheses_notes.for: Valganciclovir small RCT positive on secondary endpoints (Montoya 2013).
hypotheses_notes.against: Unreplicated; STOP-PASC found no EBV reactivation difference.

hypotheses_notes.for: Pyridostigmine single-dose iCPET effect; patients rate fluids and compression highly.
hypotheses_notes.against: Fludrocortisone RCT negative; ivabradine lowered HR without symptom benefit; no sham-controlled saline trial.

hypotheses_notes.for: Small CoQ10+NADH and oxaloacetate RCTs; rapamycin open-label with autophagy marker changes.
hypotheses_notes.against: CoQ10 alone negative in long COVID; positive supplement trials sponsor-linked and unreplicated.

hypotheses_notes.for: Large placebo responses show symptoms are modifiable by expectation and context (not specific to this hypothesis).
hypotheses_notes.against: PACE effects confined to self-report and not durable; GET rated harmful by patients; rehab worsened 42/97 in CFS_CARE.

hypotheses_notes.for: HBOT 40 sessions positive in one long-COVID RCT.
hypotheses_notes.against: HBOT 10 sessions negative in HOT-LoCO.

hypotheses_notes.for: Low-dose aripiprazole, LDN rationales; retrospective reports.
hypotheses_notes.against: LDN RCT negative for fatigue; no controlled aripiprazole data.

glossary.plain: Everyone, patients and doctors, knows who got the drug. Prone to placebo and expectation effects.
The comparison group gets a fake version of a procedure (for example blood passed through a filter that removes nothing) so no one knows who got the real thing.
Improvement in people given a dummy treatment, from expectation, natural fluctuation and enrolling when at a low point.
A 0-100 questionnaire score of physical ability; healthy adults score around 90-100, many ME/CFS patients 20-50.
Units of pressure. 1 ATA is sea-level air pressure; HBOT trials use 2.0-2.4.
Invasive cardiopulmonary exercise test: a bike test with catheters in the heart's arteries to measure filling pressures and oxygen use.
A 1991 definition of CFS needing only six months of disabling fatigue; it does not require post-exertional malaise and captures broader fatigue states.
Standardised mortality ratio: observed deaths divided by the number expected for people of the same age and sex.

key_reviews.why: Most thorough independent appraisal of GET/CBT evidence; current UK standard of care.

key_reviews.cite: Eckey 2025, PNAS: Patient-reported treatment outcomes in ME/CFS and long COVID
key_reviews.why: Largest dataset on what patients use and rate; maps treatments to symptom clusters.
Protocol-based re-analysis of the most influential behavioural trial.

key_reviews.cite: Blitshteyn 2025, Front Cell Infect Microbiol: Immunotherapies for POTS and long COVID
key_reviews.why: Overview of immune treatments and the trials still needed.

key_reviews.cite: Proal 2025, Lancet Infect Dis: Targeting the SARS-CoV-2 reservoir
key_reviews.why: Rationale for antiviral/monoclonal trials after the Paxlovid failures.

key_reviews.cite: Cairns & Hotopf 2005, Occup Med: prognosis of CFS
key_reviews.why: Still the standard systematic review of natural history.

gaps: No completed randomised trial of daratumumab, low-dose rapamycin (ME/CFS), aripiprazole or IV saline.
No trial designed for severe or very severe (bedbound) patients with home-based objective endpoints.
Almost no trial pre-specifies a biological selection marker; subgroup claims (NK cells, HLA, preload failure, illness duration) are all post hoc.
Objective outcomes (actigraphy, 2-day CPET, step counts) are rarely primary endpoints, leaving self-report vulnerable to placebo response.
Several key trials remain unpublished (BLOC/BC007, IA-PACS-CFS, Nacul LDN, RECOVER-AUTONOMIC full results, LIFT).
Long-term natural history of PEM-defined, adult-onset ME/CFS from onset (including post-COVID) beyond two years.
Systematic counting of deaths and harms (including rehab-induced deterioration) in ME/CFS.

hypotheses.name: Endothelial dysfunction
hypotheses.one_line: The lining of blood vessels fails to dilate and regulate flow, so tissues are under-supplied during effort.
hypotheses.claim: Endothelial cells normally release nitric oxide and other signals so arteries widen when tissue needs more blood. In ME/CFS this response is reported to be blunted, possibly through autoantibodies, inflammation or oxidative stress. Poor flow regulation would leave muscle and brain short of oxygen during exertion and could set off PEM. It is a mechanism layer rather than a root cause, and it could result from several upstream triggers.
predictions: Lower flow-mediated dilation and reactive hyperaemia in patients
Endothelial markers or patient IgG effects on endothelial cells in vitro
evidence_for: Flow-mediated dilation 5.1% vs 8.2% (Sandvik 2023, n=39); reduced endothelial function in CycloME substudy (Sørland 2021)
Patient IgG fragments endothelial mitochondria vs MS and healthy IgG (Prusty 2026, single lab)
Lower vessel-wall/connective-tissue proteins (ITGAV, NOTCH3, TGF-beta set) in 4 cohorts and long COVID (Solving ME/CFS re-analysis)
evidence_against: Effects are average differences with large overlap; deconditioning not always excluded
BC007 and immunoadsorption (aimed at vasoactive GPCR antibodies) failed controlled trials
Vericiguat (VERI-LONG) results not reported
decisive_tests: Within-person FMD before and during PEM versus sedentary controls
Placebo-controlled trial of a vasoactive drug with 2-day CPET endpoint

hypotheses.name: Capillary and microvascular damage
hypotheses.one_line: Capillaries in muscle and elsewhere are structurally damaged or rarefied, limiting oxygen delivery.
hypotheses.claim: Muscle biopsies show thickened capillary basement membranes and fewer capillaries, and long-COVID studies show capillary loss under the tongue and in the retina. If blood reaches the tissue but bypasses capillary beds or cannot exchange oxygen, extraction falls, as seen in the 'high-flow' iCPET phenotype. This would explain exertional intolerance unrelated to fitness. Cause could be immune, complement or viral damage to pericytes.
predictions: Basement membrane thickening and capillary rarefaction on biopsy
Improvement with treatments that repair microvasculature
evidence_for: Capillary basement membrane thickening and lower capillarisation in ME/CFS and post-COVID biopsies (Wüst group 2025 preprint)
Muscle damage, amyloid deposits and mitochondrial drop after exercise in long COVID (Appelman 2024)
Reduced oxygen extraction in preload failure (Joseph 2021)
40-session HBOT improved symptoms in one RCT (Zilberman-Itskovich 2022)
evidence_against: Biopsy studies are small and largely from one network
10-session HBOT trial negative (HOT-LoCO 2025)
decisive_tests: Blinded biopsy morphometry in large ME/CFS vs deconditioned controls
Correlation of capillary measures with 2-day CPET in the same patients

hypotheses.name: Low blood volume and preload failure
hypotheses.one_line: Too little blood returns to the heart, especially upright and during exercise, reducing cardiac output and brain flow.
hypotheses.claim: Isotope and CO-rebreathing studies show reduced plasma and red-cell volume, and invasive CPET shows low right-heart filling pressure during exercise in many patients. Upright, this lowers stroke volume and brain blood flow (seen on tilt even without POTS). It could stem from small-fibre neuropathy, low ADH/renin response, or reduced red-cell production. It explains orthostatic intolerance well; whether it explains PEM is less clear.
predictions: Symptom relief with fluids, compression and pyridostigmine
evidence_for: Preload failure common in iCPET series (Joseph 2021, n=160)
Cerebral blood flow falls on tilt in ~90% of patients (van Campen 2020)
Single-dose pyridostigmine maintained cardiac output on repeat iCPET (Joseph 2022)
Patients rate fluids and compression among the most helpful (Eckey 2025)
Low reticulocytes with adequate iron in postviral fatigue (Solving ME/CFS re-analysis, FinnGen; unreplicated)
evidence_against: Fludrocortisone negative in RCT (Rowe 2001)
Ivabradine reduced HR without symptom benefit (RECOVER-AUTONOMIC 2026)
No sham-controlled trial of IV saline
Blood-volume hormones normal in proteomics (Solving ME/CFS re-analysis)
decisive_tests: Sham-controlled IV saline crossover with function endpoints
Results of LIFT (pyridostigmine x LDN)
Blood volume measurement before/after illness onset in prospective post-COVID cohorts

hypotheses.name: Autonomic dysfunction and small-fibre neuropathy
hypotheses.one_line: Damage to small autonomic and sensory nerves impairs vascular tone, heart rate control and pain processing.
hypotheses.claim: A sizeable minority of ME/CFS and POTS patients have reduced intraepidermal nerve fibre density on skin biopsy. Loss of sympathetic fibres to veins would cause venous pooling and preload failure; sensory fibre loss would add pain. The neuropathy may be immune-mediated after infection. It is a likely contributor in a subgroup rather than a universal mechanism.
predictions: Response to IVIG in immune-mediated subgroup
evidence_for: Small-fibre neuropathy frequent in biopsied iCPET patients (Joseph 2021)
POTS and low HRV common in ME/CFS
evidence_against: IVIG negative vs albumin in autoimmune POTS (Vernino 2024)
Prevalence estimates vary widely between centres
Ivabradine trial negative for symptoms
decisive_tests: Population-representative skin biopsy study with blinded counting
IVIG trial restricted to biopsy-proven SFN with function endpoints

hypotheses.name: Viral persistence
hypotheses.one_line: Virus or viral antigen persists in tissue reservoirs and drives ongoing immune activation.
hypotheses.claim: After SARS-CoV-2 and possibly other infections, viral RNA or protein may persist in gut, lymphoid or nervous tissue. Persistent antigen would keep the immune system activated and could explain chronic symptoms. Evidence is strongest in long COVID, where viral proteins are detected months later. Whether it applies to classic ME/CFS is unknown.
evidence_for: SARS-CoV-2 antigen detected in tissue and plasma months after infection (reviewed Proal 2023)
ME/CFS incidence ~5x higher after SARS-CoV-2 (Vernon 2025)
evidence_against: Three nirmatrelvir-ritonavir RCTs null (RECOVER-VITAL 2026, STOP-PASC 2024, PAX LC 2025)
Temelimab (HERV-W) null
Antigen detected also in recovered people in some studies
decisive_tests: Trials of longer or combination antivirals and monoclonals with tissue antigen as a selection marker
Tissue antigen load vs symptom severity in matched recovered controls

hypotheses.name: Herpesvirus reactivation (EBV, HHV-6)
hypotheses.one_line: Latent herpesviruses reactivate after a trigger and drive immune and neurological dysfunction.
hypotheses.claim: EBV and HHV-6 are carried latently by most adults. In ME/CFS, abortive reactivation or high antibody responses are reported, and EBV is a common trigger of onset. Reactivated virus or its proteins (e.g. dUTPase) could activate innate immunity. Antivirals have shown modest benefit in small selected groups.
predictions: Viral DNA or early-gene antibodies elevated
Genetic predisposition to EBV control affects risk
evidence_for: Glandular fever is a strong trigger of ME/CFS in prospective cohorts
Valganciclovir RCT positive on secondary scales (Montoya 2013, n=30)
Genetically higher EBV DNA load suggestive risk factor (OR 1.59, MVP; Solving ME/CFS re-analysis)
Elevated EBV gp42 reactivity in antigen profiling (Germain 2025)
evidence_against: STOP-PASC found no EBV reactivation differences (Maestri 2025 preprint)
Antibody titres poor marker of active replication
No replicated antiviral RCT
decisive_tests: Antiviral RCT selected by viral PCR/early antigen, not IgG
Prospective serial viral load from acute infection through ME/CFS onset

hypotheses.name: Autoimmunity (functional autoantibodies)
hypotheses.one_line: Post-infectious autoantibodies, for example against adrenergic or muscarinic receptors, cause vascular and autonomic dysfunction.
hypotheses.claim: A subset of patients may develop antibodies that disturb receptor signalling or nerve function after infection, similar to other post-infectious autoimmune conditions. Female predominance, infection onset and immune genetics fit. Antibody removal or B-/plasma-cell depletion should then help. Recent controlled trials have narrowed the GPCR version, while plasma-cell depletion and IgG transfer keep a broader version alive.
predictions: Benefit from antibody removal or plasma-cell depletion
evidence_for: Daratumumab 6/10 sustained responders with IgG fall (Fluge 2025, open-label)
Long-COVID IgG transfers pain hypersensitivity to mice (Chen 2026; Mignolet 2026)
Cyclophosphamide 55% open-label response with HLA association (Rekeland 2020)
evidence_against: Rituximab phase III negative (Fluge 2019)
Immunoadsorption no better than sham (IAMPOCO, IA-PACS-CFS 2026)
No GPCR autoantibody elevation on REAP/Luminex, q>0.68 (Germain 2025)
BC007 company trial negative (2024)
decisive_tests: Randomised placebo-controlled daratumumab trial
IgG transfer from ME/CFS (non-COVID) patients with blinded readouts
Pre-specified antibody-selected sham-controlled trial

hypotheses.name: Immune (T-cell) exhaustion
hypotheses.one_line: Chronic antigen stimulation leaves CD8 T cells and NK cells exhausted and less able to clear infection.
hypotheses.claim: Exhausted T cells express inhibitory receptors and lose function after prolonged stimulation. In ME/CFS, single-cell and epigenetic data suggest CD8 T cells are primed toward exhaustion, and NK cytotoxicity is reduced. This fits with a persistent antigen or reactivating virus. It may be consequence rather than cause.
predictions: Exhaustion markers (PD-1, TOX) on T cells
evidence_for: CD8 T cells transcriptionally primed toward exhaustion (Iu 2024, PNAS)
T-cell exhaustion signals in NIH deep phenotyping (Walitt 2024)
Low NK count predicted non-response to daratumumab (Fluge 2025)
evidence_against: Immune cell, methylation and repertoire data give few reproducible signals across cohorts (Solving ME/CFS re-analysis)
NK cytotoxicity findings vary by assay
decisive_tests: Replication of exhaustion signatures in independent cohorts
Longitudinal tracking from infection to ME/CFS onset

hypotheses.name: Innate immune hyperactivation
hypotheses.one_line: Ongoing activation of monocytes, interferon and cytokine pathways sustains symptoms.
hypotheses.claim: Cytokine profiles differ early in ME/CFS, with an activated pattern in the first three years that later fades. Persistent interferon or inflammasome activity could cause sickness symptoms and metabolic shifts. Effects in blood are inconsistent across studies.
evidence_for: Distinct cytokine signatures early in illness (Hornig 2015, n=298)
Complement and myeloid activation in long COVID (Cervia-Hasler 2024)
evidence_against: Cytokine findings poorly replicated across ME/CFS cohorts
Methylprednisolone trial in long COVID stopped early without benefit (PoCoVIT 2026)
Prednisolone/losartan negative (Myoflame-19 2026)
decisive_tests: Standardised longitudinal cytokine/interferon panels from onset
Targeted anti-cytokine RCT in a biomarker-defined subgroup

hypotheses.name: Complement activation and thromboinflammation
hypotheses.one_line: Chronic complement activation damages vessel lining and platelets, so clotting and inflammation feed each other.
hypotheses.claim: The terminal complement complex is persistently activated in active long COVID, with signs of haemolysis, platelet activation and monocyte-platelet aggregates. This could injure endothelium and capillaries. It is the best-replicated blood abnormality in long COVID but is less studied in classic ME/CFS.
predictions: Raised sC5b-9 and complement split products
evidence_for: Cervia-Hasler 2024 (Science), replicated in outline by Baillie 2024, Klein 2023, Barratt-Due 2024
Higher C3 and complement variants reported in ME/CFS (CDC; Solving ME/CFS re-analysis)
evidence_against: One adjusted null replication (Farztdinov preprint)
No complement inhibitor trial yet
Limited ME/CFS data
decisive_tests: Complement inhibitor RCT in biomarker-positive long COVID
Complement measures in non-COVID ME/CFS cohorts

hypotheses.name: Fibrin amyloid microclots
hypotheses.one_line: Fibrinolysis-resistant amyloid fibrin(ogen) microclots block capillaries and trap inflammatory molecules.
hypotheses.claim: Fluorescence microscopy of platelet-poor plasma shows amyloid microclots, reported in long COVID and ME/CFS. They could obstruct capillaries and reduce oxygen delivery. Anticoagulant 'triple therapy' was promoted on this basis. The method is difficult to standardise and independent labs disagree.
evidence_for: Pretorius 2021 and later papers from the same network
evidence_against: STOP-PASC found no microclot differences vs controls (Maestri 2025 preprint)
Assay not standardised; few independent replications
No RCT of anticoagulation for microclots; bleeding risk
decisive_tests: Blinded multi-lab microclot quantification on shared samples
Placebo-controlled trial with microclot endpoints

hypotheses.name: Cell danger response (Naviaux)
hypotheses.one_line: Cells stuck in a protective low-energy 'danger' state after a threat fail to complete the healing cycle.
hypotheses.claim: The cell danger response (CDR) is a conserved metabolic reaction to threat in which mitochondria shift from energy production to defence, with extracellular ATP (purinergic) signalling. Naviaux proposes that ME/CFS is a persistent CDR, a hypometabolic state like dauer. His 2016 metabolomics found most altered metabolites decreased, consistent with hypometabolism. Antipurinergic drugs such as suramin are the proposed test.
evidence_for: Naviaux 2016 PNAS: 80% of altered metabolites decreased (n=45 vs 39)
Rapamycin responders show purine metabolism changes (Gile 2026)
evidence_against: Metabolomic findings vary across cohorts; Hoel/Germain datasets do not show uniform hypometabolism
No ME/CFS trial of suramin
decisive_tests: Low-dose suramin RCT in ME/CFS
Replication of hypometabolic signature with standardised fasting samples

hypotheses.name: Mitochondrial / energy metabolism impairment
hypotheses.one_line: Cells cannot produce energy normally, especially during exertion, causing early lactate and PEM.
hypotheses.claim: Several lines suggest impaired pyruvate dehydrogenase, Complex V inefficiency or reduced oxidative capacity. This would force early reliance on glycolysis and slow recovery. It may be intrinsic or secondary to poor perfusion or circulating factors.
predictions: Abnormal mitochondrial respiration in patient cells
evidence_for: Amino-acid pattern implying impaired PDH (Fluge 2016, n=200 vs 102)
Complex V inefficiency in lymphoblasts (Missailidis 2020)
Post-exercise mitochondrial enzyme drop in long COVID muscle (Appelman 2024)
Aromatic lactate deficit across 5 cohorts (Solving ME/CFS re-analysis)
evidence_against: Serum effect on myoblast respiration failed replication at n=120 (Ryback/Ponting 2026)
CoQ10 alone negative in long COVID
Supplement trials small and sponsor-linked
decisive_tests: Muscle 31P-MRS and biopsy respiration before/after PEM vs deconditioned controls
Independent replication of lymphoblast Complex V defect

hypotheses.name: IDO metabolic trap (Phair, Davis)
hypotheses.one_line: A bistable tryptophan-kynurenine circuit, set by IDO1/IDO2 variants and substrate inhibition, flips into a persistent low-tryptophan state.
hypotheses.claim: IDO1 converts tryptophan to kynurenine and is inhibited by high tryptophan. Combined with a deleterious IDO2 variant, a mathematical model predicts two stable states, one of which traps cells with low tryptophan and serotonin and high kynurenine after an inflammatory trigger. Exiting the trap would need a perturbation. It is a mathematical model with limited direct data.
evidence_for: Preliminary OMF data on IDO2 variants (unpublished/limited)
Altered tryptophan metabolites in some metabolomic studies
evidence_against: DecodeME GWAS did not highlight IDO loci
Mendelian randomisation finds no causal effect of kynurenine on ME/CFS risk (Solving ME/CFS re-analysis)
Plasma kynurenine findings inconsistent
decisive_tests: Intracellular tryptophan/kynurenine measurement in patient cells with IDO genotypes
Test of predicted bistability in culture

hypotheses.name: HPA axis blunting
hypotheses.one_line: The stress-hormone axis is under-active, with low cortisol and enhanced feedback.
hypotheses.claim: Mild hypocortisolism, a flattened diurnal rhythm and enhanced negative feedback are reported in ME/CFS. This is probably a consequence of illness, inactivity or sleep disturbance rather than a cause, but it could amplify symptoms. Low-dose hydrocortisone had small effects and suppressed the adrenal axis.
evidence_for: Repeated reports of mild hypocortisolism (2026 meta-analysis per atlas)
Cleare 1999 hydrocortisone 5-10 mg: 28% vs 9% improved
evidence_against: McKenzie 1998 hydrocortisone RCT: adrenal suppression, little benefit
Changes small and nonspecific
decisive_tests: Longitudinal cortisol from pre-illness in prospective cohorts

hypotheses.name: Pituitary / vasopressin deficiency
hypotheses.one_line: Low ADH (vasopressin) secretion despite concentrated blood leads to fluid loss and low blood volume.
hypotheses.claim: A 2025 study reported undetectable vasopressin in most patients despite high plasma osmolality. If true, this would explain polyuria, thirst and low blood volume, and suggest desmopressin for a subgroup. DecodeME tissue enrichment pointing to pituitary gives indirect support.
evidence_for: Vasopressin undetectable in 82% in an uncontrolled 2025 series
DecodeME genetic signal enriched in brain and pituitary tissues
evidence_against: Uncontrolled, assay concerns
Desmopressin evidence only acute in POTS (Coffin 2012)
decisive_tests: Controlled copeptin study with water deprivation/hypertonic saline testing

hypotheses.name: Neuroinflammation (microglial activation)
hypotheses.one_line: Activated microglia and astrocytes in the brain produce fatigue, cognitive problems and pain.
hypotheses.claim: PET and MR spectroscopy studies suggest brain inflammation in ME/CFS and long COVID. Inflammation in brainstem or limbic regions could generate sickness behaviour and PEM. Results conflict and tracer studies are small.
evidence_for: Nakatomi 2014 TSPO PET positive (n=9)
Long-COVID TSPO increase (VanElzakker 2024)
Raised ventricular lactate (Shungu/Mathew)
evidence_against: Raijmakers 2022 TSPO PET negative
James (Stanford) 2026: no brain TSPO signal, strong muscle signal
LDN fatigue RCT negative (2026)
decisive_tests: Large multi-tracer PET studies with standardised analysis
CSF inflammatory markers vs matched controls

hypotheses.name: Brainstem and craniocervical instability
hypotheses.one_line: Brainstem dysfunction, sometimes from craniocervical instability or Chiari, disrupts autonomic and arousal control.
hypotheses.claim: Some patients, often with hypermobility, are reported to have craniocervical instability or intracranial hypertension compressing the brainstem. Surgery has been followed by improvement in case series. Imaging studies of brainstem volume and connectivity are small. This may explain a minority subgroup at most.
evidence_for: Case series of fusion surgery improvement
Bragée 2020: CCI and intracranial hypertension common in a referral sample
evidence_against: No controlled trial; surgery high risk
Imaging criteria not standardised; selection bias
decisive_tests: Blinded imaging comparing ME/CFS with matched hypermobile controls
Prospective registry of surgical outcomes with controls

hypotheses.name: Persistent sickness behaviour / vagal signalling
hypotheses.one_line: The brain's sickness response, normally triggered by infection signals (e.g. via the vagus), stays switched on.
hypotheses.claim: During infection, cytokines signal to the brain and cause fatigue, malaise and withdrawal. If a local infection or inflammation near the vagus nerve persists, or the brain's set point changes, sickness behaviour could persist. This frames many symptoms but is hard to test directly.
predictions: Vagal or brainstem markers of immune signalling
Symptoms reduced by blocking cytokine signalling
evidence_for: Symptoms closely resemble sickness behaviour
Post-infectious onset common
evidence_against: Anti-inflammatory trials negative in long COVID
Direct evidence of vagal infection absent
decisive_tests: Vagal nerve imaging/biopsy studies; vagal stimulation RCTs with sham

hypotheses.name: Gut dysbiosis
hypotheses.one_line: Altered gut microbiota and barrier function drive immune activation and metabolic changes.
hypotheses.claim: Butyrate producers such as Faecalibacterium prausnitzii are reduced in ME/CFS, and short-duration patients show stronger dysbiosis. Microbial products may affect immunity and metabolism. A synbiotic improved several long-COVID symptoms in one trial. Dysbiosis could also be a consequence of illness, diet and inactivity.
evidence_for: Reduced butyrate producers (Guo 2023, n=106 vs 91)
Dysbiosis stronger early (Xiong 2023)
R. gnavus/F. plautii overgrowth replicates and explains low IPA (Solving ME/CFS re-analysis)
SIM01 synbiotic positive in long COVID (Lau 2024, n=463)
evidence_against: MR finds no causal effect of IPA and related metabolites (Solving ME/CFS re-analysis)
Aromatic lactate deficit not explained by gut bacteria (Solving ME/CFS re-analysis)
Faecal transplant data anecdotal
decisive_tests: Replication of SIM01-type trial in ME/CFS
Prospective microbiome sampling before onset

hypotheses.name: Genetic susceptibility acting through neurons
hypotheses.one_line: Inherited variants affecting nervous-system genes raise risk, pointing to brain-based mechanisms.
hypotheses.claim: DecodeME (15,579 cases) found genome-wide significant loci, with tissue enrichment in brain and pituitary rather than immune tissues. The overall genetic signal replicates in the Million Veteran Program and FinnGen. Candidate genes include pain-sensitisation and immune-response genes. Genetics marks susceptibility, not necessarily the ongoing mechanism.
predictions: Mendelian randomisation links to specific proteins
evidence_for: DecodeME 2025 loci; tissue enrichment brain/pituitary
Genetic correlation rg 0.73 with MVP; EPHB1 and CLEC3B replicate by MR (Solving ME/CFS re-analysis)
evidence_against: Most individual loci not yet replicated
Small effect sizes; heritability modest
decisive_tests: Independent GWAS replication of individual loci
Functional studies of implicated genes

hypotheses.name: Circulating (serum) factor
hypotheses.one_line: Something in patient blood, such as IgG or exosomes, impairs healthy cells.
hypotheses.claim: Several experiments put patient plasma or serum onto healthy cells and observed altered impedance, respiration, mitochondrial morphology or muscle force. If replicated, this would point to a transferable factor and allow bioassays. The best-known muscle mitochondrial version failed a well-powered replication in 2026.
predictions: Patient plasma alters healthy cells reproducibly
evidence_for: Plasma-swap nanoneedle impedance (Esfandyarpour 2019, n=20 vs 20)
IgG fragments endothelial mitochondria vs MS and healthy IgG (Prusty 2026)
Long-COVID IgG transfers symptoms to mice (Chen 2026)
evidence_against: Ryback/Ponting 2026: no serum effect on myoblast respiration (n=67 vs 53, d≥0.52 excluded)
IBEC 3D muscle study n=4/5/4 with pseudoreplication risk
Nanoneedle unreplicated in peer review
decisive_tests: Multi-lab blinded serum bioassay with disease controls and PEM-timed samples
IgG depletion and rescue experiments

hypotheses.name: Sodium-calcium overload in muscle (Wirth & Scheibenbogen)
hypotheses.one_line: Under-perfused muscle accumulates sodium and then calcium via the sodium-calcium exchanger, damaging mitochondria and causing PEM.
hypotheses.claim: The model proposes that beta2-adrenergic dysfunction (perhaps via autoantibodies) and vasoconstriction reduce muscle blood flow. Hypoxic muscle relies on glycolysis; protons are exported by NHE1, loading the cell with sodium, which reverses the sodium-calcium exchanger and raises intracellular calcium, injuring mitochondria. This cycle explains delayed, prolonged PEM and suggests drugs that block NHE1 or reduce sodium loading. Elements are testable with 23Na-MRI.
predictions: Calcium overload and mitochondrial damage after exertion
Benefit from NHE1 inhibitors or vasodilators
evidence_for: Higher muscle sodium on 23Na-MRI (Petter 2022, 6 vs 6)
Post-exertional muscle damage and mitochondrial drop (Appelman 2024)
Endothelial dysfunction findings
evidence_against: Upstream GPCR-antibody step weakened by negative antigen profiling and failed IA/BC007 trials
Sodium MRI sample tiny
No interventional test yet
decisive_tests: Larger 23Na-MRI studies before and after exertion vs deconditioned controls
Pilot trial of NHE1 inhibition

hypotheses.name: Mast cell activation
hypotheses.one_line: Inappropriate mast-cell mediator release causes flushing, tachycardia, GI and cognitive symptoms.
hypotheses.claim: Mast cell activation syndrome overlaps clinically with POTS, hypermobility and ME/CFS. Histamine and other mediators could cause vasodilation and orthostatic symptoms. Treatment with H1/H2 antihistamines is common. Diagnostic criteria are contested and data are observational.
evidence_for: Observational improvement with H1+H2 blockers in long COVID (Glynne 2022)
Clinical overlap with POTS/hEDS
evidence_against: No RCTs; mediator tests rarely positive
Diagnostic criteria inconsistent
decisive_tests: RCT of antihistamines with mediator-defined selection

hypotheses.name: Connective tissue / hypermobility
hypotheses.one_line: Hypermobility and connective-tissue weakness predispose to venous pooling, instability and dysautonomia.
hypotheses.claim: Joint hypermobility is more common in ME/CFS and POTS. Lax connective tissue in veins could worsen pooling, and in the neck could contribute to craniocervical problems. Lower blood levels of vessel-wall/extracellular-matrix proteins have been reported.
evidence_for: Hypermobility overrepresented in clinic samples
Lower ITGAV/NOTCH3/TGF-beta set proteins (Solving ME/CFS re-analysis)
evidence_against: Clinic-based selection; population data lacking
No mechanism-specific treatment
decisive_tests: Population-based hypermobility prevalence in ME/CFS
Venous compliance measurement

hypotheses.name: Cornell integrated multi-omics model (Hanson)
hypotheses.one_line: PEM reflects a maladaptive multi-system response to exertion visible across immune, metabolic and proteomic layers.
hypotheses.claim: Using 2-day CPET with blood sampling, the Cornell group reports that patients fail to mount and resolve normal exercise responses in plasma proteins, metabolites and immune cells, with CD8 T-cell exhaustion features. They frame ME/CFS as an integrated failure of recovery across systems rather than a single lesion. The model is descriptive and generates leads rather than one causal claim.
predictions: Divergent post-exertion trajectories vs sedentary controls
evidence_for: Plasma proteome maladaptation after exertion in 79 vs 53 (Germain 2025, Mol Cell Proteomics)
CD8 exhaustion priming (Iu 2024)
evidence_against: Re-analysis of the 2022 metabolomics: within-person exercise responses barely differ; 'growing divergence' does not hold (Solving ME/CFS re-analysis, PEM)
Clean negative autoantibody profiling from the same group (Germain 2025) narrows immune explanations
decisive_tests: Pre-registered within-person analyses in a new 2-day CPET cohort
Matching deconditioned and disease controls

hypotheses.name: Open Medicine Foundation models (Davis, Xiao, Systrom)
hypotheses.one_line: A cluster of OMF-funded models: a circulating plasma factor, the IDO metabolic trap, and neurovascular preload failure.
hypotheses.claim: OMF has backed several ideas rather than one: plasma-swap nanoneedle evidence for a blood factor; the IDO metabolic trap; and Systrom's neurovascular dysregulation with preload failure, tested by pyridostigmine. Its data centre and the 2025 treatment survey aim to link subgroups to treatments. The common thread is a measurable, possibly reversible physiological state.
evidence_for: Nanoneedle plasma-swap (Esfandyarpour 2019)
Pyridostigmine single-dose iCPET RCT (Joseph 2022)
Patient survey subgroups (Eckey 2025)
evidence_against: No peer-reviewed nanoneedle replication
IDO trap not supported by GWAS/MR
Longer pyridostigmine trial in long COVID negative (2025 abstract)
decisive_tests: LIFT trial results
Independent replication of nanoneedle assay

hypotheses.name: Multisystem post-infectious model (Komaroff & Lipkin reviews)
hypotheses.one_line: ME/CFS and long COVID share a set of biological abnormalities across brain, immune, energy and vascular systems, triggered by infection.
hypotheses.claim: Two influential reviews catalogue overlapping findings: neuroinflammation, immune activation and exhaustion, autoantibodies, impaired energy metabolism, endothelial and autonomic dysfunction, and gut dysbiosis. They argue the two illnesses are variants of the same post-infectious process and that research on each informs the other. It is a synthesis, not a single falsifiable mechanism.
predictions: Shared abnormalities between ME/CFS and long COVID
evidence_for: Treatment ratings correlate between ME/CFS and long COVID (R²=0.68; Eckey 2025)
Post-COVID ME/CFS incidence data (Vernon 2025)
evidence_against: Many catalogued abnormalities are unreplicated or contested individually
Breadth makes the model hard to falsify
decisive_tests: Head-to-head cohorts with identical assays in ME/CFS, long COVID and recovered controls

hypotheses.name: Altered 'effort preference' (NIH)
hypotheses.one_line: Patients choose fewer hard-effort options in a decision task, which the NIH team interpreted as a defining feature rather than fatigue or weakness.
proponents: Walitt, Nath and the NIH intramural team
hypotheses.claim: In deep phenotyping of 17 post-infectious ME/CFS patients, participants chose the hard task less often in the Effort-Expenditure for Rewards Task, and the authors proposed altered effort preference linked to low CSF catecholamines and motor-network changes. They framed fatigue as arising from brain integrative circuits. Critics argue the task was not validated in ME/CFS and that choosing less effort is a rational response to PEM, not a preference.
predictions: Reduced hard-task choices independent of capacity
Brain activity differences during effort tasks
evidence_for: Fewer hard-task choices (Walitt 2024, n=17 vs 21)
Low CSF catecholamines and altered motor-cortex activity in the same study
evidence_against: Tiny sample; task not validated; PEM-avoidance alternative explanation
Patients and many researchers objected to the framing; findings not replicated
decisive_tests: Replication with tasks that separate anticipated PEM cost from motivation
Compare with other disabling illnesses with exertional limits

hypotheses.name: Psychosomatic / cognitive-behavioural (fear-avoidance) model
hypotheses.one_line: An initial illness is perpetuated by unhelpful beliefs, activity avoidance and deconditioning, so CBT and graded exercise should reverse it.
hypotheses.claim: The model holds that after a trigger, beliefs that activity is harmful lead to avoidance, deconditioning and symptom focus, maintaining disability. It predicted that CBT and graded exercise would produce recovery. PACE and Dutch trials reported modest self-reported benefits. The model is now widely disputed: objective outcomes were null and PEM is not explained by beliefs.
predictions: CBT/GET produce recovery including on objective measures
evidence_for: PACE: modest self-reported fatigue and function gains with CBT/GET at 52 weeks (White 2011)
Belief/attribution associated with prognosis in older cohorts (Cairns & Hotopf 2005)
Large placebo responses show context and expectation affect symptom reports
evidence_against: Effects confined to self-report and not durable at 2.5 years (Sharpe 2015; Wilshire 2018)
NICE 2021 rated evidence low/very low and advised against GET
Patients rate GET most harmful (Eckey 2025); rehab worsened 42/97 (CFS_CARE 2026)
Reproducible biological differences (2-day CPET, genetics, muscle pathology) not explained by beliefs
Critique of the model's evidence base (Geraghty 2019)

hypotheses.name: Deconditioning
hypotheses.one_line: Exercise intolerance is simply loss of fitness from inactivity.
proponents: Implicit in rehabilitation models; early long-COVID exercise studies
hypotheses.claim: If symptoms reflect detraining, patients should look like sedentary controls on exercise testing, recover normally between tests, and improve with graded training. Deconditioning certainly coexists in severe illness. The question is whether it explains the disease.
evidence_for: Lower peak VO2 in patients is partly explained by fitness
Some long-COVID CPET studies attributed limitation to deconditioning
evidence_against: Day-2 CPET decline in many patients, not seen in sedentary controls (Keller 2024, n=84; memory)
Post-exertional muscle damage and mitochondrial drop not explained by fitness (Appelman 2024)
iCPET shows preload failure and poor extraction atypical of detraining (Joseph 2021, 2023 review)
Lower muscle proteins in blood not explained by steps or lying time (Solving ME/CFS re-analysis)
GET harmful in surveys
decisive_tests: Matched-activity controls (bedrest or immobilised volunteers) on 2-day CPET and biopsy
